```sql
WITH month_txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS ym,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS deposits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS withdrawals
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE strftime('%Y', txn_date) = '2020'
  GROUP BY customer_id, ym
),
month_balances AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    ym,
    deposits - withdrawals AS month_end_balance
  FROM month_txns
),
month_positive_counts AS (
  SELECT
    ym,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS positive_count
  FROM month_balances
  WHERE month_end_balance > 0
  GROUP BY ym
),
extreme_months AS (
  SELECT
    'max' AS tag,
    ym,
    positive_count
  FROM month_positive_counts
  WHERE positive_count = (SELECT MAX(positive_count) FROM month_positive_counts)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'min' AS tag,
    ym,
    positive_count
  FROM month_positive_counts
  WHERE positive_count = (SELECT MIN(positive_count) FROM month_positive_counts)
  LIMIT 2
),
month_avgs AS (
  SELECT
    e.tag,
    e.ym,
    AVG(b.month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
  FROM extreme_months e
  JOIN month_balances b ON b.ym = e.ym
  GROUP BY e.tag, e.ym
)
SELECT
  (SELECT avg_balance FROM month_avgs WHERE tag = 'max') -
  (SELECT avg_balance FROM month_avgs WHERE tag = 'min') AS avg_balance_difference,
  (SELECT ym FROM month_avgs WHERE tag = 'max') AS month_highest_positive_customers,
  (SELECT avg_balance FROM month_avgs WHERE tag = 'max') AS avg_balance_highest,
  (SELECT ym FROM month_avgs WHERE tag = 'min') AS month_lowest_positive_customers,
  (SELECT avg_balance FROM month_avgs WHERE tag = 'min') AS avg_balance_lowest
;

WITH cohort AS (
    SELECT
        l.id_bioguide,
        MIN(lt.term_start) AS first_term_start
    FROM
        legislators l
        JOIN legislators_terms lt ON l.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
    WHERE
        DATE(lt.term_start) BETWEEN '1917-01-01' AND '1999-12-31'
    GROUP BY
        l.id_bioguide
),
periods AS (
    SELECT 1 AS period
    UNION ALL SELECT 2
    UNION ALL SELECT 3
    UNION ALL SELECT 4
    UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6
    UNION ALL SELECT 7
    UNION ALL SELECT 8
    UNION ALL SELECT 9
    UNION ALL SELECT 10
    UNION ALL SELECT 11
    UNION ALL SELECT 12
    UNION ALL SELECT 13
    UNION ALL SELECT 14
    UNION ALL SELECT 15
    UNION ALL SELECT 16
    UNION ALL SELECT 17
    UNION ALL SELECT 18
    UNION ALL SELECT 19
    UNION ALL SELECT 20
),
cohort_size AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM cohort
),
retention AS (
    SELECT
        p.period,
        COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_bioguide) AS retained
    FROM periods p
    CROSS JOIN cohort c
    LEFT JOIN legislators_terms lt
      ON lt.id_bioguide = c.id_bioguide
      AND DATE(lt.term_start) <= DATE(c.first_term_start, '+' || p.period || ' years', '-1 day')
      AND DATE(lt.term_end) >= DATE(c.first_term_start, '+' || p.period || ' years', '-1 day')
    WHERE lt.id_bioguide IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY p.period
)
SELECT
    p.period,
    COALESCE(r.retained, 0) AS retained_legislators,
    cs.total AS cohort_size,
    ROUND(COALESCE(r.retained, 0)*1.0/cs.total, 4) AS retention_rate
FROM periods p
CROSS JOIN cohort_size cs
LEFT JOIN retention r ON p.period = r.period
ORDER BY p.period

    SELECT
        l.id AS legislator_id,
        MIN(lt.start_date) AS first_term_start
    FROM
        legislators l
        JOIN legislators_terms lt ON l.id = lt.legislator_id
    WHERE
        DATE(lt.start_date) BETWEEN '1917-01-01' AND '1999-12-31'
    GROUP BY
        l.id
),
periods AS (
    -- Generate numbers 1 through 20 for period years
    SELECT 1 AS period
    UNION ALL SELECT 2
    UNION ALL SELECT 3
    UNION ALL SELECT 4
    UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6
    UNION ALL SELECT 7
    UNION ALL SELECT 8

    UNION ALL SELECT 10
    UNION ALL SELECT 11
    UNION ALL SELECT 12
    UNION ALL SELECT 13
    UNION ALL SELECT 14
    UNION ALL SELECT 15
    UNION ALL SELECT 16
    UNION ALL SELECT 17
    UNION ALL SELECT 18
    UNION ALL SELECT 19
    UNION ALL SELECT 20
),
cohort_size AS (
    -- Total size of the cohort
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM cohort
),
retention_calc AS (
    SELECT
        p.period,
        COUNT(DISTINCT c.legislator_id) AS retained_count
    FROM
        periods p
        CROSS JOIN cohort c
        LEFT JOIN legislators_terms lt
            ON lt.legislator_id = c.legislator_id
            AND DATE(lt.start_date) <= DATE(c.first_term_start, '+' || p.period || ' years', '-1 day')
            AND DATE(lt.end_date) >= DATE(c.first_term_start, '+' || p.period || ' years', '-1 day')
    GROUP BY
        p.period, c.legislator_id
    HAVING
        MAX(CASE WHEN lt.legislator_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
),
retention_by_period AS (
    SELECT
        p.period,
        COUNT(r.retained_count) AS retained
    FROM periods p
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT c.legislator_id, rc.period
        FROM cohort c
        JOIN periods rc ON 1=1
        LEFT JOIN legislators_terms lt
            ON lt.legislator_id = c.legislator_id
            AND DATE(lt.start_date) <= DATE(c.first_term_start, '+' || rc.period || ' years', '-1 day')
            AND DATE(lt.end_date) >= DATE(c.first_term_start, '+' || rc.period || ' years', '-1 day')
        WHERE lt.legislator_id IS NOT NULL
    ) r ON r.period = p.period
    GROUP BY p.period
)
SELECT
    p.period,
    COALESCE(rbp.retained, 0) AS retained_legislators,
    cs.total AS cohort_size,
    ROUND(COALESCE(rbp.retained * 1.0, 0) / cs.total, 4) AS retention_rate
FROM
    periods p
    CROSS JOIN cohort_size cs
    LEFT JOIN retention_by_period rbp ON p.period = rbp.period
ORDER BY
    p.period

WITH pizza_assign AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id, 
        pizza_id, 
        CASE WHEN pizza_id = 1 THEN 'Meatlovers' ELSE 'Vegetarian' END AS pizza_name
    FROM pizza_customer_orders
),
standard_toppings AS (
    SELECT 
        r.pizza_id, t.topping_name
    FROM pizza_recipes r
    JOIN pizza_toppings t ON ',' || r.toppings || ',' LIKE '%,' || t.topping_id || ',%'
),
order_exclusions AS (
    SELECT order_id, topping_id
    FROM pizza_get_exclusions
),
order_extras AS (
    SELECT order_id, topping_id
    FROM pizza_get_extras
),
order_ingredients AS (
    SELECT 
        o.row_id,
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        pa.pizza_name,
        t.topping_name,
        'standard' AS src
    FROM pizza_customer_orders o
    JOIN pizza_assign pa ON o.order_id = pa.order_id AND o.pizza_id = pa.pizza_id
    JOIN standard_toppings t ON pa.pizza_id = t.pizza_id
    LEFT JOIN order_exclusions e ON o.order_id = e.order_id AND t.topping_name = (SELECT topping_name FROM pizza_toppings WHERE topping_id = e.topping_id)
    WHERE e.topping_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        o.row_id,
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        pa.pizza_name,
        t.topping_name,
        'extra' AS src
    FROM pizza_customer_orders o
    JOIN pizza_assign pa ON o.order_id = pa.order_id AND o.pizza_id = pa.pizza_id
    JOIN order_extras e ON o.order_id = e.order_id
    JOIN pizza_toppings t ON e.topping_id = t.topping_id
),
ingred_cnts AS (
    SELECT row_id, order_id, customer_id, pizza_name, topping_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM order_ingredients
    GROUP BY row_id, order_id, customer_id, pizza_name, topping_name
),
joined_names AS (
    SELECT 
        row_id, order_id, customer_id, pizza_name,
        GROUP_CONCAT(
            CASE WHEN cnt > 1 THEN '2x' || topping_name ELSE topping_name END
            , '||' -- temp sep
        ) AS toppings
    FROM (
        SELECT *, 
               CASE WHEN cnt > 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END as ord1, 
               topping_name as ord2
        FROM ingred_cnts
    )
    GROUP BY row_id, order_id, customer_id, pizza_name
)
SELECT 
    o.row_id, o.order_id, o.customer_id, j.pizza_name, 
    j.pizza_name || ': ' || 
    TRIM(REPLACE(
        (
         SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(val, ', ')
         FROM (
            SELECT val FROM (
                SELECT  
                  CASE WHEN cnt > 1 THEN '2x' || topping_name ELSE topping_name END as val,
                  CASE WHEN cnt > 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END as ord1,
                  topping_name as ord2
                FROM ingred_cnts ic
                WHERE ic.row_id = o.row_id AND ic.order_id = o.order_id AND ic.pizza_name = j.pizza_name
            )
            ORDER BY ord1, ord2
          )
        ), ', ', '')
    ) AS final_ingredients
FROM pizza_customer_orders o
JOIN joined_names j ON o.row_id = j.row_id AND o.order_id = j.order_id AND o.pizza_name = j.pizza_name
GROUP BY o.row_id, o.order_id, o.customer_id, j.pizza_name
ORDER BY o.row_id ASC;

        pco.row_id,
        pco.order_id,
        pco.customer_id,
        CASE WHEN pco.pizza_id = 1 THEN 'Meatlovers' ELSE 'Vegetarian' END AS pizza_name,
        pco.pizza_id,
        pco.order_time
    FROM pizza_customer_orders pco
),
standard_toppings AS (
    SELECT pr.pizza_id, pt.topping_name, pt.topping_id
    FROM pizza_recipes pr

      ON ',' || pr.toppings || ',' LIKE '%,' || pt.topping_id || ',%'
),
order_exclusions AS (

    FROM pizza_get_exclusions
),
order_extras AS (
    SELECT order_id, extras AS topping_id
    FROM pizza_get_extras
),
ordered_ingredients AS (
    -- standard toppings (minus exclusions)
    SELECT pa.row_id, pa.order_id, pa.customer_id, pa.pizza_name, pa.order_time, st.topping_name, st.topping_id, 'standard' AS src
    FROM pizza_assign pa
    JOIN standard_toppings st ON pa.pizza_id = st.pizza_id
    LEFT JOIN order_exclusions oe ON pa.order_id = oe.order_id AND st.topping_id = oe.topping_id
    WHERE oe.topping_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- extras
    SELECT pa.row_id, pa.order_id, pa.customer_id, pa.pizza_name, pa.order_time, pt.topping_name, pt.topping_id, 'extra' AS src
    FROM pizza_assign pa
    JOIN order_extras ex ON pa.order_id = ex.order_id
    JOIN pizza_toppings pt ON ex.topping_id = pt.topping_id
),

WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_purchase_timestamp
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
),
customer_order_stats AS (
    SELECT
        do.customer_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT do.order_id) AS frequency,
        MAX(do.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_purchase,
        SUM(oi.price + oi.freight_value) AS monetary
    FROM delivered_orders do
    JOIN order_items oi ON do.order_id = oi.order_id
    GROUP BY do.customer_id
),
reference_date AS (
    -- Use latest delivered order as the reference for recency calculation
    SELECT MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS max_date FROM delivered_orders
),
customer_rfm_raw AS (
    SELECT
        cos.customer_id,
        JULIANDAY((SELECT max_date FROM reference_date)) - JULIANDAY(cos.last_purchase) AS recency_days,
        cos.frequency,
        cos.monetary
    FROM customer_order_stats cos
),
rfm_scores AS (
    -- Assign R, F, M scores (1 = best, 5 = worst) using quintiles
    SELECT
        r.*,
        NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY recency_days ASC) AS recency_score,
        NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS frequency_score,
        NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY monetary DESC) AS monetary_score
    FROM customer_rfm_raw r
),
rfm_segments AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        (recency_score) || (frequency_score) || (monetary_score) AS rfm_cell,
        CASE
            -- Champions
            WHEN recency_score = 1 AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 1 AND 4
                THEN 'Champions'
            -- Can't Lose Them
            WHEN (recency_score = 4 OR recency_score = 5) AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 1 AND 2
                THEN "Can't Lose Them"
            -- Hibernating
            WHEN (recency_score = 4 OR recency_score = 5) AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 3 AND 6
                THEN 'Hibernating'
            -- Lost
            WHEN (recency_score = 4 OR recency_score = 5) AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 7 AND 10
                THEN 'Lost'
            -- Loyal Customers
            WHEN (recency_score = 2 OR recency_score = 3) AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 1 AND 4
                THEN 'Loyal Customers'
            -- Needs Attention
            WHEN recency_score = 3 AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 5 AND 6
                THEN 'Needs Attention'
            -- Recent Users
            WHEN recency_score = 1 AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 7 AND 8
                THEN 'Recent Users'
            -- Potential Loyalists
            WHEN (recency_score = 1 AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 5 AND 6)
               OR (recency_score = 2 AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 5 AND 8)
                THEN 'Potential Loyalists'
            -- Price Sensitive
            WHEN recency_score = 1 AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 9 AND 10
                THEN 'Price Sensitive'
            -- Promising
            WHEN recency_score = 2 AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 9 AND 10
                THEN 'Promising'
            -- About to Sleep
            WHEN recency_score = 3 AND (frequency_score + monetary_score) BETWEEN 7 AND 10
                THEN 'About to Sleep'
            ELSE 'Other'
        END AS rfm_segment
    FROM rfm_scores
),
customer_avg_sales AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_unique_id,
        r.rfm_segment,
        r.monetary,
        r.frequency,
        CASE WHEN r.frequency > 0 THEN CAST(r.monetary AS FLOAT)/r.frequency ELSE NULL END AS avg_sales_per_order
    FROM rfm_segments r
    JOIN customers c ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
)
SELECT
    rfm_segment,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS customer_count,
    AVG(avg_sales_per_order) AS avg_sales_per_order
FROM customer_avg_sales
WHERE rfm_segment != 'Other'
GROUP BY rfm_segment
ORDER BY avg_sales_per_order DESC;
```

According to the RFM definition document, calculate the average sales per order for each customer within distinct RFM segments, considering only 'delivered' orders. Use the customer unique identifier. Clearly define how to calculate Recency based on the latest purchase timestamp and specify the criteria for classifying RFM segments. The average sales should be computed as the total spend divided by the total number of orders. Please analyze and report the differences in average sales across the RFM segments

Provided benchmark documentation:
# Introduction to the RFM Model

The RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) model segments and scores customers based on three key dimensions:

• Recency (R): How long it has been since the customer’s last purchase. A lower R score (e.g., R = 1) indicates a very recent purchase, while a higher R score (e.g., R = 5) indicates a longer time since the last purchase.

• Frequency (F): How often the customer purchases within a given time period. A lower F score (e.g., F = 1) signifies that the customer buys very frequently, whereas a higher F score (e.g., F = 5) indicates less frequent purchasing.

• Monetary (M): The total amount of money the customer spends. A lower M score (e.g., M = 1) indicates higher overall spending, while a higher M score (e.g., M = 5) signifies lower spending over the measured period.

Each customer’s R, F, and M scores are determined by their respective percentiles when compared to other customers. By concatenating the three scores, you get an “RFM cell”—for instance, a customer with R=1, F=5, and M=2 would fall into the 152 segment.

# RFM Segmentation Calculation

After scoring customers on Recency, Frequency, and Monetary values, the next step is to group them into segments that require different marketing or sales strategies. Typically:

1. Determine each customer’s recency score (R) from 1 to 5 (1 = very recent purchase, 5 = not recent).  
2. Determine each customer’s frequency score (F) from 1 to 5 (1 = most frequent purchases, 5 = least frequent).  
3. Determine each customer’s monetary score (M) from 1 to 5 (1 = highest spending, 5 = lowest spending).  
4. Concatenate these three scores into an RFM score (e.g., 153, 514).

By analyzing the distribution of RFM scores and placing them into buckets—for example, “Champions,” “Loyal Customers,” “At Risk,” “Lost,” etc.—you can tailor marketing, sales, and retention strategies to maximize the potential of each segment. 

For instance, a “Champion” (R=1, F=1, M=1) is a recent, frequent, and high-spending user who is highly valuable to your business, whereas a “Lost” customer (e.g., R=5, F=5, M=5) may require re-engagement offers or might no longer be cost-effective to target. Different segments can thus be prioritized based on their profitability and likelihood of responding positively to marketing efforts.

## RFM Segmentation Logic

Customers are assigned to specific segments (RFM Buckets) based on a combination of their Recency, Frequency, and Monetary scores. The segmentation logic is as follows:

- **Champions**: Customers who have made a recent purchase, with high frequency and high monetary value. These are considered the most valuable customers.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 4.

- **Can't Lose Them**: Previously frequent and high-spending customers who have not made a recent purchase. These customers are at risk of leaving and need attention.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 2.

- **Hibernating**: Customers whose last purchase was a while ago, with low to moderate frequency and spending. These customers might have lost interest in the products.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 3 and 6.

- **Lost**: Customers who have not purchased in a long time and have low frequency and monetary value. These customers are likely lost.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 10.

- **Loyal Customers**: Customers who are frequent buyers with decent spending levels, and they have made a purchase relatively recently. These customers are likely to be very loyal.
  - Criteria: Recency = 2 or 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 4.

- **Needs Attention**: Customers whose purchase frequency and spending are moderate. They haven't bought very recently, but they could be incentivized to become more active.
  - Criteria: Recency = 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 6.

- **Recent Users**: Customers who made a purchase recently, but their frequency and spending are moderate. These are relatively new or inconsistent buyers.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 8.

- **Potential Loyalists**: Customers who show potential to become loyal customers. They have good frequency and monetary scores, and they have made recent purchases. With the right engagement, they could become loyal customers.
  - Criteria:
    - Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 6.
    - OR Recency = 2 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 8.

- **Price Sensitive**: Customers who have made recent purchases but tend to spend less, indicating they may be more sensitive to price.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 9 and 10.

- **Promising**: These customers exhibit high potential with decent frequency and monetary scores, and they could become more valuable over time.
  - Criteria: Recency = 2 and Frequency + Monetary score between 9 and 10.

- **About to Sleep**: Customers whose frequency and spending are low, and their last purchase was some time ago. These customers are likely to become inactive.
  - Criteria: Recency = 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 10.

## Summary

This segmentation logic groups customers based on their behavior in terms of when they last purchased (Recency), how often they purchase (Frequency), and how much they spend (Monetary). By understanding which group a customer belongs to, organizations can tailor marketing strategies to engage the right audience more effectively, improving customer retention and maximizing value.

WITH seller_product_sales AS (
  SELECT
    oi.seller_id,
    p.product_category_name,
    COUNT(*) AS total_products_sold,
    SUM(oi.price) AS total_sales,
    AVG(oi.price) AS avg_item_price
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY oi.seller_id, p.product_category_name
),
seller_agg AS (
  SELECT
    sps.seller_id,
    (
      SELECT pct.product_category_name_english
      FROM seller_product_sales sps2
      JOIN product_category_name_translation pct ON sps2.product_category_name = pct.product_category_name
      WHERE sps2.seller_id = sps.seller_id
      ORDER BY sps2.total_products_sold DESC, sps2.product_category_name
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS top_category_english,
    SUM(sps.total_sales) AS total_sales,
    AVG(sps.avg_item_price) AS avg_item_price,
    SUM(sps.total_products_sold) AS total_products_sold
  FROM seller_product_sales sps
  GROUP BY sps.seller_id
  HAVING SUM(sps.total_products_sold) > 100
),
seller_reviews AS (
  SELECT
    oi.seller_id,
    AVG(r.review_score * 1.0) AS avg_review_score
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN order_reviews r ON oi.order_id = r.order_id
  GROUP BY oi.seller_id
),
seller_packing_times AS (
  SELECT
    oi.seller_id,
    AVG(
      JULIANDAY(oi.shipping_limit_date) - JULIANDAY(o.order_purchase_timestamp)
    ) AS avg_packing_days
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY oi.seller_id
)
SELECT
  sa.seller_id,
  sa.total_sales,
  sa.avg_item_price,
  sr.avg_review_score,
  spt.avg_packing_days,
  sa.total_products_sold,
  sa.top_category_english AS highest_sales_category_english
FROM seller_agg sa
LEFT JOIN seller_reviews sr ON sa.seller_id = sr.seller_id
LEFT JOIN seller_packing_times spt ON sa.seller_id = spt.seller_id

WITH monthly_sales_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS year_month,
    product_id,
    SUM(amount) AS total_sales
  FROM orderlines
  JOIN orders ON orderlines.order_id = orders.order_id
  WHERE product_id IN (4160, 7790)
    AND order_date >= '2016-01-01'
    AND order_date < '2019-01-01'
  GROUP BY product_id, year_month
  ORDER BY product_id, year_month
),
-- Assign row numbers to each month within each product
sales_with_rownum AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY year_month) AS rn
  FROM monthly_sales_filtered
),
-- Calculate Centered Moving Average (CMA) for months 7 to 30 using two overlapping 12-month windows for each product
cma_calc AS (
  SELECT
    s1.product_id,
    s1.year_month,
    s1.total_sales,
    s1.rn,
    -- First window: 5 before, self, 6 after
    (SELECT AVG(s2.total_sales)
      FROM sales_with_rownum s2
      WHERE s2.product_id = s1.product_id
        AND s2.rn BETWEEN s1.rn - 5 AND s1.rn + 6
    ) AS cma1,
    -- Second window: 6 before, self, 5 after
    (SELECT AVG(s2.total_sales)
      FROM sales_with_rownum s2
      WHERE s2.product_id = s1.product_id
        AND s2.rn BETWEEN s1.rn - 6 AND s1.rn + 5
    ) AS cma2
  FROM sales_with_rownum s1
),
cma_final AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    (IFNULL(cma1,0) + IFNULL(cma2,0))/2.0 AS CMA
  FROM cma_calc
  WHERE rn BETWEEN 7 AND 30
),
-- Calculate sales-to-CMA ratio, and average seasonality adjustment per month of year for each product
seasonality_index AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    CAST(strftime('%m', year_month || '-01') AS INTEGER) AS month,
    AVG(total_sales / NULLIF(CMA,0)) AS avg_seasonal_ratio
  FROM cma_final
  GROUP BY product_id, month
),
-- Prepare regression data for each product, using total_sales/CMA for months 7 to 30 (seasonal adjusted actuals)
regression_data AS (
  SELECT
    cf.product_id,
    cf.rn,
    cf.total_sales / NULLIF(si.avg_seasonal_ratio,0) AS deseasonalized_sales
  FROM cma_final cf
  JOIN seasonality_index si
    ON cf.product_id = si.product_id
    AND CAST(strftime('%m', cf.year_month || '-01') AS INTEGER) = si.month
),
-- Weighted linear regression for each product: x=rn (time), y=deseasonalized_sales, weights=1 (equal, can be improved)
reg_stats AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    SUM(rn) AS sum_x,
    SUM(deseasonalized_sales) AS sum_y,
    SUM(rn * rn) AS sum_x2,
    SUM(rn * deseasonalized_sales) AS sum_xy
  FROM regression_data
  GROUP BY product_id
),
-- Compute regression coefficients for each product
regression_coeffs AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    -- Slope
    (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x) AS slope,
    -- Intercept
    (sum_y - ((n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x)) * sum_x) / n AS intercept
  FROM reg_stats
),
-- Forecast for months 37 to 48 (2018.01~2018.12 corresponds to steps 37-48 for a 2016.01 start)
forecast_months AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    rn AS forecast_rn,
    strftime('%m', date('2016-01-01', '+'||(rn-1)||' months')) AS forecast_month
  FROM (
    SELECT 4160 AS product_id UNION ALL SELECT 7790
  ) prod
  JOIN (
    SELECT rn FROM (SELECT 37 AS rn UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40
                   UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44
                   UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48)
  ) seq
),
-- Join for coefficients and forecast deseasonalized sales
forecast_calc AS (
  SELECT
    f.product_id,
    f.forecast_rn,
    (rc.intercept + rc.slope * f.forecast_rn) AS deseasonalized_forecast,
    CAST(f.forecast_month AS INTEGER) AS month
  FROM forecast_months f
  JOIN regression_coeffs rc ON f.product_id = rc.product_id
),
-- Apply seasonality index to get final forecast including seasonality
final_forecast AS (
  SELECT
    fc.product_id,
    fc.forecast_rn,
    fc.deseasonalized_forecast,
    si.avg_seasonal_ratio,
    fc.deseasonalized_forecast * si.avg_seasonal_ratio AS final_seasonal_forecast
  FROM forecast_calc fc
  JOIN seasonality_index si ON fc.product_id = si.product_id AND fc.month = si.month
)
SELECT
  product_id,
  AVG(final_seasonal_forecast) AS avg_2018_forecasted_annual_sales
FROM final_forecast
GROUP BY product_id
;
```

# Explanation of Metrics

## 1. Sales-to-CMA Ratio
- **Definition**: This ratio compares actual sales to the centered moving average (CMA) of sales.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Centered Moving Average (CMA)**: The CMA is a smoothed value of sales calculated over a rolling 12-month period. It averages sales from the months before and after a given month, specifically using two overlapping windows (5 months before and 6 months after, and vice versa).
  - **Sales-to-CMA Ratio**: The ratio is computed by dividing the actual sales amount for a month by its corresponding CMA value. A ratio greater than 2 indicates that the actual sales are more than twice the smoothed average for that period, suggesting significantly higher-than-average sales.

## 2. 12-Month Overlapping Windows
- **Definition**: A method to smooth sales data over time by averaging values in a specified window.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Window Size**: The window spans 12 months, with the specific approach involving overlapping periods. 
  - **First Window**: For a given month, this window includes 5 months before and 6 months after.
  - **Second Window**: Another window includes 6 months before and 5 months after the given month.
  - **Averaging**: Sales data is averaged over these two overlapping windows to compute the CMA. This method smooths out fluctuations by considering both the past and future sales in the calculation.

## 3. Restriction to the 7th and 30th Months
- **Definition**: A filter applied to focus calculations within a specific range of months.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Time Range**: Only the months between the 7th and 30th time steps (which correspond to specific periods) are considered for calculating the CMA and ratio.
  - **Purpose**: This restriction is used to avoid edge effects in the data where the moving average might be less reliable (e.g., at the very beginning or end of the available data). By focusing on these months, the calculations are more stable and meaningful.

    ) AS distance_km

# Flight Route Distance Calculation

## Introduction

This document describes the method used to calculate the distance between two cities for flight routes. The calculation is based on the Haversine formula, which is commonly used to find the shortest distance between two points on a sphere given their latitude and longitude. This method is especially useful for determining flight distances between airports located in different cities around the world.

## City and Coordinate Extraction

For each flight, the following data is obtained:

- **Departure city** (referred to as `from_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).
- **Arrival city** (referred to as `to_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).

The coordinates are extracted as decimal values, with longitude and latitude represented in degrees. This ensures that trigonometric operations can be applied during the distance calculation.

## Haversine Formula

The Haversine formula is used to calculate the great-circle distance between two points on a sphere using their latitude and longitude. The formula is given as:

\[
d = 2r \cdot \arcsin\left(\sqrt{\sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) + \cos(\phi_1) \cdot \cos(\phi_2) \cdot \sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \lambda}{2}\right)}\right)
\]

Where:

- \( d \) is the distance between the two points (in kilometers).
- \( r \) is the radius of the Earth (approximately 6371 km).
- \( \phi_1 \) and \( \phi_2 \) are the latitudes of the departure and arrival points, respectively, in radians.
- \( \Delta \phi = \phi_2 - \phi_1 \) is the difference in latitudes.
- \( \lambda_1 \) and \( \lambda_2 \) are the longitudes of the departure and arrival points, respectively, in radians.
- \( \Delta \lambda = \lambda_2 - \lambda_1 \) is the difference in longitudes.

### Conversion to Radians

Since the input coordinates are in degrees, they must be converted to radians before applying the Haversine formula. This conversion is done using the formula:

\[
\text{radians} = \text{degrees} \times \frac{\pi}{180}
\]

## Symmetry of Routes

To identify unique flight routes between two cities, we standardize the order of cities in each route. Specifically, we ensure that the lexicographically smaller city name is always listed as the first city (`city1`), and the larger city is listed as the second city (`city2`). This ensures that a flight from City A to City B is treated the same as a flight from City B to City A.

## Average Route Distance

Once the distances for all flights between two cities are computed, the average distance for each city pair is calculated by summing the distances and dividing by the total number of flights between those cities:

\[
\text{Average Distance} = \frac{\sum \text{Flight Distances}}{\text{Number of Flights}}
\]

## Conclusion

This method of flight route distance calculation provides a reliable way to determine the great-circle distance between cities based on the coordinates of their respective airports. The use of the Haversine formula ensures accurate results for distances on the Earth's surface, making it ideal for aviation and travel analysis.

WITH yearly_causes AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y', collision_date) AS year,
    primary_collision_factor,
    COUNT(*) AS count
  FROM collisions
  GROUP BY year, primary_collision_factor
),
ranked_causes AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    primary_collision_factor,
    count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY count DESC) AS rnk
  FROM yearly_causes
),
year_top2 AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    GROUP_CONCAT(primary_collision_factor, '|') AS top2_factors
  FROM ranked_causes
  WHERE rnk <= 2
  GROUP BY year
),
mode_top2 AS (
  SELECT
    top2_factors,
    COUNT(*) AS freq
  FROM year_top2
  GROUP BY top2_factors
  ORDER BY freq DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT y.year
FROM year_top2 y
JOIN mode_top2 m
  ON y.top2_factors <> m.top2_factors
```

WITH yearly_causes AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y', collision_date) AS year,
    primary_collision_factor,
    COUNT(*) AS count
  FROM collisions
  GROUP BY year, primary_collision_factor
),

  SELECT
    year,
    primary_collision_factor,
    count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY count DESC) AS rnk
  FROM yearly_causes
),
year_top2 AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    GROUP_CONCAT(primary_collision_factor, '|') AS top2_factors
  FROM ranked_causes
  WHERE rnk <= 2
  GROUP BY year
),
mode_top2 AS (
  SELECT
    top2_factors,
    COUNT(*) AS freq
  FROM year_top2
  GROUP BY top2_factors
  ORDER BY freq DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT y.year
FROM year_top2 y
JOIN mode_top2 m
  ON y.top2_factors <> m.top2_factors

WITH durations AS (
  SELECT
    Track.TrackId,
    Track.Name,
    Track.Milliseconds / 60000.0 AS minutes
  FROM Track
),
stats AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(minutes) AS min_time,
    MAX(minutes) AS max_time,
    AVG(minutes) AS avg_time,
    (MIN(minutes) + AVG(minutes)) / 2.0 AS mid_min_avg,
    (AVG(minutes) + MAX(minutes)) / 2.0 AS mid_avg_max
  FROM durations
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    d.TrackId,
    d.Name,
    d.minutes,
    CASE
      WHEN d.minutes >= s.min_time AND d.minutes < s.mid_min_avg THEN 'Short'
      WHEN d.minutes >= s.mid_min_avg AND d.minutes < s.mid_avg_max THEN 'Medium'
      WHEN d.minutes >= s.mid_avg_max AND d.minutes <= s.max_time THEN 'Long'
    END AS duration_category
  FROM durations d
  CROSS JOIN stats s
),
min_max_by_cat AS (
  SELECT
    duration_category,
    MIN(minutes) AS min_minutes,
    MAX(minutes) AS max_minutes
  FROM classified
  GROUP BY duration_category
),
revenue_by_cat AS (
  SELECT
    c.duration_category,
    SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS total_revenue
  FROM classified c
  LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.TrackId = c.TrackId
  GROUP BY c.duration_category
)
SELECT
  mm.duration_category,
  mm.min_minutes,
  mm.max_minutes,
  COALESCE(rbc.total_revenue, 0) AS total_revenue
FROM min_max_by_cat mm
LEFT JOIN revenue_by_cat rbc
  ON mm.duration_category = rbc.duration_category
ORDER BY
  CASE mm.duration_category
    WHEN 'Short' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Long' THEN 3
    ELSE 4
  END

# Special Words Definition

## Batting Average
- Batting average is a measure of a batsman's performance, calculated by dividing the total number of runs scored by the number of times they have been dismissed. A higher batting average indicates a more consistent and successful batsman.
- Batting Average = Total Runs ÷ Total Dismissals

## Strike Rate
- In batting, strike rate indicates the scoring rate of a batsman, showing the average number of runs scored per 100 balls faced. A higher strike rate reflects an aggressive and fast-scoring batsman.
- Strike Rate = (Total Runs ÷ Balls Faced) × 100

## Wickets Taken
- Wickets taken refers to the total number of times a bowler has successfully dismissed an opposing batsman. This statistic is a core measure of a bowler's effectiveness and impact on the game.

## Economy Rate
- Economy rate measures a bowler's efficiency by indicating the average number of runs conceded per over (6 balls) bowled. A lower economy rate shows greater control and efficiency in restricting the opposition's scoring.
- Economy Rate = (Total Runs Conceded ÷ Balls Bowled) × 6

## Wickets Taken
- The number of times a bowler successfully dismisses a batsman in a single match.  This metric is a direct indicator of the bowler's effectiveness, showing how many players they were able to remove from play.

## Runs Given
- The total number of runs scored by the batting side off a particular bowler’s deliveries in a single match.  This value reflects the runs the bowler has conceded to the batting team, and a lower runs-given value is typically favorable for the bowler's performance.

WITH toy_products AS (
    SELECT product_id
    FROM products
    WHERE product_category_name IN (
        SELECT product_category_name
        FROM product_category_name_translation
        WHERE product_category_name_english LIKE '%toy%'
    )
),
daily_sales AS (
    SELECT
        date(o.order_purchase_timestamp, 'start of day') AS sale_date,
        SUM(oi.price) AS total_sales
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE oi.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM toy_products)
      AND date(o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2018-08-29'
      AND o.order_status IN ('delivered', 'shipped')
    GROUP BY sale_date
),
date_series AS (
    SELECT date('2017-01-01', '+' || (n) || ' days') AS series_date
    FROM (
        SELECT row_number() OVER () - 1 AS n
        FROM (SELECT 1 FROM orders LIMIT 600)
    )
    WHERE series_date BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2018-08-29'
),
regression_stats AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS n,
        SUM(x) AS sum_x,
        SUM(y) AS sum_y,
        SUM(x * y) AS sum_xy,
        SUM(x * x) AS sum_xx
    FROM (
        SELECT
            CAST(julianday(ds.series_date) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS x,
            COALESCE(ds2.total_sales, 0) AS y
        FROM date_series ds
        LEFT JOIN daily_sales ds2 ON ds.series_date = ds2.sale_date
    )
),
regression_coeffs AS (
    SELECT
        (sum_xy - (sum_x * sum_y) * 1.0 / n) / (sum_xx - (sum_x * sum_x) * 1.0 / n) AS b,
        (sum_y - ((sum_xy - (sum_x * sum_y) * 1.0 / n) / (sum_xx - (sum_x * sum_x) * 1.0 / n)) * sum_x) * 1.0 / n AS a
    FROM regression_stats
),
predict_dates AS (
    SELECT date('2018-12-05', '+' || n || ' days') AS pred_date
    FROM (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3)
),
symmetric_window AS (
    SELECT pd.pred_date, date(pd.pred_date, '-' || offset || ' days') AS window_date
    FROM predict_dates pd
    JOIN (SELECT -2 AS offset UNION ALL SELECT -1 UNION ALL SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2) off
),
date_x_values AS (
    SELECT
        window_date,
        CAST(julianday(window_date) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS INTEGER) AS x
    FROM (
        SELECT DISTINCT window_date FROM symmetric_window
    )
),
window_predictions AS (
    SELECT
        sw.pred_date,
        sw.window_date,
        rc.a + rc.b * dx.x AS predicted_sales
    FROM symmetric_window sw
    JOIN date_x_values dx ON sw.window_date = dx.window_date
    CROSS JOIN regression_coeffs rc
),
moving_avg_5d AS (
    SELECT
        pred_date,
        AVG(predicted_sales) AS movavg_5d
    FROM window_predictions
    GROUP BY pred_date
)
SELECT SUM(movavg_5d) AS sum_of_5d_moving_averages
FROM moving_avg_5d
WHERE pred_date BETWEEN '2018-12-05' AND '2018-12-08';

WITH first_five_laps AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT race_id, lap
    FROM lap_positions
    WHERE lap BETWEEN 1 AND 5
),
driver_lap_positions AS (
    SELECT
        lp.race_id,
        lp.lap,
        lp.driver_id,
        lp.position,
        LAG(lp.position) OVER (
            PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id ORDER BY lp.lap
        ) as prev_position
    FROM lap_positions lp
    JOIN first_five_laps ffl ON lp.race_id = ffl.race_id AND lp.lap = ffl.lap
),
potential_overtakes AS (
    SELECT
        dl1.race_id,
        dl1.lap,
        dl1.driver_id AS overtaker_id,
        dl1.position AS overtaker_pos,
        dl2.driver_id AS overtaken_id,
        dl2.position AS overtaken_pos,
        dl1.prev_position AS overtaker_prev,
        dl2.prev_position AS overtaken_prev
    FROM driver_lap_positions dl1
    JOIN driver_lap_positions dl2
        ON dl1.race_id = dl2.race_id
        AND dl1.lap = dl2.lap
        AND dl1.position + 1 = dl2.position
        AND dl1.prev_position > dl2.prev_position
    WHERE dl1.prev_position IS NOT NULL AND dl2.prev_position IS NOT NULL
),
retirements_lap AS (
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap FROM retirements WHERE lap IS NOT NULL
),
pitstops_thislap AS (
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap FROM pit_stops
),
pitstops_prev_lap AS (
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap+1 AS lap FROM pit_stops
),
grid_positions AS (
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, grid FROM results
),
overtake_classified AS (
    SELECT
        po.race_id,
        po.lap,
        CASE
            -- Retirement
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM retirements_lap r
                WHERE r.race_id = po.race_id AND r.driver_id = po.overtaken_id AND r.lap = po.lap
            ) THEN 'R'
            -- Pit entry
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM pitstops_thislap p
                WHERE p.race_id = po.race_id AND p.driver_id = po.overtaken_id AND p.lap = po.lap
            ) THEN 'P'
            -- Pit exit
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM pitstops_prev_lap p
                WHERE p.race_id = po.race_id AND p.driver_id = po.overtaken_id AND p.lap = po.lap
            ) THEN 'P'
            -- Start related (lap 1, grid diff <= 2)
            WHEN po.lap = 1 AND EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM grid_positions g1
                JOIN grid_positions g2
                    ON g1.race_id = g2.race_id
                WHERE g1.race_id = po.race_id
                  AND g1.driver_id = po.overtaker_id
                  AND g2.driver_id = po.overtaken_id
                  AND ABS(g1.grid - g2.grid) <= 2
            ) THEN 'S'
            -- Standard Track Overtake
            ELSE 'T'
        END AS category
    FROM potential_overtakes po
)
SELECT
    category,
    COUNT(*) AS overtake_count
FROM overtake_classified
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category;

        LAG(lp.position) OVER (PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id ORDER BY lp.lap) AS prev_position
    FROM lap_positions lp
    JOIN first_five_laps ff ON lp.race_id = ff.race_id AND lp.lap = ff.lap
),
candidate_overtakes AS (
    SELECT
        d1.race_id,
        d1.lap,
        d1.driver_id AS overtaker_id,
        d1.position AS overtaker_pos,
        d2.driver_id AS overtaken_id,
        d2.position AS overtaken_pos,
        d2.prev_position AS overtaken_prev,
        d1.prev_position AS overtaker_prev
    FROM driver_changes d1
    JOIN driver_changes d2 ON
        d1.race_id = d2.race_id AND
        d1.lap = d2.lap AND
        d1.position + 1 = d2.position AND
        d1.prev_position > d2.prev_position
    WHERE
        d1.position < d1.prev_position
),
retirements_on_lap AS (
    SELECT r.race_id, r.driver_id, r.lap
    FROM retirements r
),
pitstops_this_lap AS (
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap
    FROM pit_stops
),
pitstops_prev_lap AS (
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap+1 AS lap_exit
    FROM pit_stops
),
race_grids AS (
    SELECT ra.race_id, d.driver_id, ra.grid
    FROM results ra
    JOIN drivers d ON ra.driver_id = d.driver_id
),
overtake_classified AS (
    SELECT
        c.race_id,
        c.lap,
        CASE
            -- 1. Retirement
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM retirements_on_lap r
                WHERE r.race_id = c.race_id AND r.driver_id = c.overtaken_id AND r.lap = c.lap
            ) THEN 'R'
            -- 2. Pit in
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM pitstops_this_lap p
                WHERE p.race_id = c.race_id AND p.driver_id = c.overtaken_id AND p.lap = c.lap
            ) THEN 'P'
            -- 2. Pit out (previous lap)
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM pitstops_prev_lap p
                WHERE p.race_id = c.race_id AND p.driver_id = c.overtaken_id AND p.lap_exit = c.lap
            ) THEN 'P'
            -- 3. Start overtake
            WHEN c.lap = 1 AND EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM race_grids g1
                JOIN race_grids g2 ON g1.race_id = g2.race_id
                WHERE g1.race_id = c.race_id AND g1.driver_id = c.overtaker_id AND g2.driver_id = c.overtaken_id
                AND ABS(g1.grid - g2.grid) <= 2
            ) THEN 'S'
            -- 4. Track pass
            ELSE 'T'
        END AS overtake_type
    FROM candidate_overtakes c
)
SELECT
    overtake_type,
    COUNT(*) AS overtake_count
FROM overtake_classified
GROUP BY overtake_type
ORDER BY overtake_type;

In the first five laps of the race, how many overtakes occurred in each category—retirements, pit stops, start-related overtakes, and standard on-track passes?

Provided benchmark documentation:
# Overtake Label Classification

In racing, overtakes are categorized into different states based on specific conditions, reflecting the circumstances in which the overtaking occurred. Below are the classifications and their detailed explanations:

## 1. R (Retirement) - Overtake during Retirement
An overtake is labeled as **R (Retirement)** if the overtaken driver retired on the same lap as the overtake. This indicates that the overtake occurred just before or during the overtaken driver's retirement, meaning they could no longer continue the race after that lap.

## 2. P (Pit) - Overtake related to Pit Stops
An overtake is classified as **P (Pit)** under two scenarios:
   - **Pit Entry**: If the overtake occurred while the overtaken driver was entering the pit lane, and the driver pitted on the same lap, it indicates that the overtaking happened due to the overtaken driver reducing speed to enter the pit lane.
   - **Pit Exit**: If the overtake occurred as the overtaken driver was exiting the pit lane, especially if the driver pitted on the previous lap and the time gap between the drivers was less than a typical pit stop duration. This suggests that the overtake happened while the overtaken driver was potentially at a lower speed, rejoining the race track from the pit lane.

## 3. S (Start) - Overtake at Race Start
If the overtake took place on the first lap of the race, and the two drivers were within two grid positions of each other at the start, the overtake is classified as **S (Start)**. This classification indicates that the overtake was part of the initial racing shuffle during the race's launch phase, where close position changes are common.

## 4. T (Track) - Overtake under Normal Racing Conditions
If none of the above conditions apply, the overtake is categorized as **T (Track)**, meaning it occurred during normal racing conditions on the track, without any external factors like pit stops or retirements influencing the outcome. This is the default classification for overtakes that happen during regular competition.

---

These classifications help to identify and record the context of each overtake with clarity, ensuring accurate representation of race dynamics.

WITH filtered_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        m.month_year,
        m.interest_id,
        m.composition,
        m.index_value,
        (CASE WHEN m.index_value != 0 THEN m.composition * 1.0 / m.index_value ELSE NULL END) AS avg_composition
    FROM interest_metrics m
    WHERE (m._year > 2018 OR (m._year = 2018 AND m._month >= 9))
      AND (m._year < 2019 OR (m._year = 2019 AND m._month <= 8))
),
max_monthly_interest AS (
    SELECT 
        fm.month_year,
        fm.interest_id,
        fm.avg_composition,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY fm.month_year ORDER BY fm.avg_composition DESC) AS rn
    FROM filtered_metrics fm
),

        mm.month_year,
        im.interest_name,
        mm.avg_composition AS max_index_composition
    FROM max_monthly_interest mm
    JOIN interest_map im ON mm.interest_id = im.id
    WHERE mm.rn = 1
),
rolling_max AS (
    SELECT 
        mp.month_year,
        mp.interest_name,
        mp.max_index_composition,
        LAG(mp.interest_name, 1) OVER (ORDER BY mp.month_year) AS prev_1_interest_name,
        LAG(mp.max_index_composition, 1) OVER (ORDER BY mp.month_year) AS prev_1_max_index_composition,

        AVG(mp.max_index_composition) OVER (ORDER BY mp.month_year ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_3mo_avg
    FROM max_per_month mp
)
SELECT 
    month_year AS date,
    interest_name,
    max_index_composition,
    rolling_3mo_avg,
    prev_1_interest_name, prev_1_max_index_composition,
    prev_2_interest_name, prev_2_max_index_composition
FROM rolling_max
ORDER BY month_year

WITH finished_orders_per_month AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_created_year AS year,
    o.order_created_month AS month,
    o.delivery_order_id AS hub_id,
    COUNT(*) AS finished_order_count
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.order_status = 'finished'
    AND ((o.order_created_year = 2023 AND o.order_created_month = 2)
         OR (o.order_created_year = 2023 AND o.order_created_month = 3))
  GROUP BY o.order_created_year, o.order_created_month, o.delivery_order_id
),
feb_orders AS (
  SELECT hub_id, finished_order_count
  FROM finished_orders_per_month
  WHERE year = 2023 AND month = 2
),
mar_orders AS (
  SELECT hub_id, finished_order_count
  FROM finished_orders_per_month
  WHERE year = 2023 AND month = 3
)
SELECT
  h.hub_id,
  h.hub_name,
  f.finished_order_count AS feb_finished_orders,
  m.finished_order_count AS mar_finished_orders,
  ROUND(100.0 * (m.finished_order_count - f.finished_order_count) / NULLIF(f.finished_order_count,0), 2) AS percent_increase
FROM mar_orders m
JOIN feb_orders f ON m.hub_id = f.hub_id
JOIN hubs h ON h.hub_id = m.hub_id
WHERE (m.finished_order_count - f.finished_order_count) > 0
  AND 1.0 * (m.finished_order_count - f.finished_order_count) / NULLIF(f.finished_order_count,0) > 0.2
ORDER BY percent_increase DESC;

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE expanded_packaging AS (
  -- Each packaging and the contents it directly contains
  SELECT
    pr.packaging_id AS root_packaging_id,
    pr.contains_id AS leaf_packaging_id,
    pr.qty AS factor
  FROM packaging_relations pr

  UNION ALL

  -- Expand: for each child that is also a parent, go deeper
  SELECT
    ep.root_packaging_id,
    pr.contains_id,
    ep.factor * pr.qty AS factor
  FROM expanded_packaging ep
  JOIN packaging_relations pr ON ep.leaf_packaging_id = pr.packaging_id
)
, leaf_packaging AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT pr.contains_id
  FROM packaging_relations pr
  LEFT JOIN packaging_relations as parent_pr ON pr.contains_id = parent_pr.packaging_id
  WHERE parent_pr.packaging_id IS NULL
)
, packaging_totals AS (
  SELECT ep.root_packaging_id, SUM(ep.factor) AS total_qty
  FROM expanded_packaging ep
  JOIN leaf_packaging l ON ep.leaf_packaging_id = l.contains_id
  GROUP BY ep.root_packaging_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_qty) AS average_leaf_quantity_per_final_packaging
FROM packaging_totals

calls.content:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE packaging_expansion AS (
  -- Start with all packaging: each row is a packaging id, referencing a 'parent' (package) and 'child' (sub-package or product), and the quantity of child in parent
  SELECT
    pr.parent_packaging_id AS root_packaging_id,
    pr.child_packaging_id,
    pr.quantity AS factor
  FROM packaging_relations pr

  UNION ALL

  -- Recursively expand child packaging until we reach leaf packaging (not referenced as a parent in packaging_relations)
  SELECT
    pe.root_packaging_id,
    pr.child_packaging_id,
    pe.factor * pr.quantity
  FROM packaging_expansion pe
  JOIN packaging_relations pr
    ON pe.child_packaging_id = pr.parent_packaging_id
)
-- Find packaging items that never act as 'parent' (i.e., are leaf nodes)
, leaf_packaging AS (
   SELECT DISTINCT child_packaging_id
   FROM packaging_relations
   WHERE child_packaging_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT parent_packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
)
-- For each root packaging (final packaging combination), sum all fully expanded leaf quantities
, packaging_totals AS (
  SELECT
    pe.root_packaging_id,
    SUM(pe.factor) AS total_qty
  FROM packaging_expansion pe
  JOIN leaf_packaging l ON pe.child_packaging_id = l.child_packaging_id
  GROUP BY pe.root_packaging_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_qty) AS average_leaf_quantity_per_final_packaging
FROM packaging_totals;
```

WITH whsle AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', whsle_date) AS year,
        c.category_name,
        v."whsle_px_rmb-kg" AS wholesale_price,
        v.item_code
    FROM veg_whsle_df v
    JOIN veg_cat c ON v.item_code = c.item_code
    WHERE strftime('%Y', whsle_date) BETWEEN '2020' AND '2023'
),
loss_data AS (
    SELECT
        item_code,
        ROUND(AVG("loss_rate_%"), 2) AS avg_loss_rate
    FROM veg_loss_rate_df
    GROUP BY item_code
),
agg AS (
    SELECT
        w.year,
        w.category_name,
        ROUND(AVG(w.wholesale_price), 2) AS avg_wholesale_price,
        ROUND(MAX(w.wholesale_price), 2) AS max_wholesale_price,
        ROUND(MIN(w.wholesale_price), 2) AS min_wholesale_price,
        ROUND(MAX(w.wholesale_price) - MIN(w.wholesale_price), 2) AS wholesale_price_difference,
        ROUND(SUM(w.wholesale_price), 2) AS total_wholesale_price,
        -- Selling price = wholesale_price * (1 + avg_loss_rate/100)
        ROUND(SUM(w.wholesale_price * (1 + IFNULL(l.avg_loss_rate,0)/100)), 2) AS total_selling_price,
        ROUND(AVG(IFNULL(l.avg_loss_rate,0)), 2) AS avg_loss_rate,
        ROUND(SUM(w.wholesale_price * IFNULL(l.avg_loss_rate,0)/100), 2) AS total_loss,
        ROUND(SUM(w.wholesale_price * (1 + IFNULL(l.avg_loss_rate,0)/100)) - SUM(w.wholesale_price), 2) AS profit
    FROM
        whsle w
        LEFT JOIN loss_data l ON w.item_code = l.item_code
    GROUP BY w.year, w.category_name
)
SELECT 
    year,
    category_name AS category,
    avg_wholesale_price,
    max_wholesale_price,
    min_wholesale_price,
    wholesale_price_difference,
    total_wholesale_price,
    total_selling_price,
    avg_loss_rate,
    total_loss,
    profit
FROM agg
ORDER BY year, category;

WITH all_teams_league AS (
  SELECT t.id AS team_id, t.team_long_name, l.id AS league_id, l.name AS league_name
  FROM Team t
  CROSS JOIN League l
),
team_wins AS (
  SELECT
    m.league_id,
    m.home_team_api_id AS team_id,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal THEN 1 END) AS wins
  FROM Match m
  GROUP BY m.league_id, m.home_team_api_id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    m.league_id,
    m.away_team_api_id AS team_id,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal THEN 1 END) AS wins
  FROM Match m
  GROUP BY m.league_id, m.away_team_api_id
),
total_team_wins AS (
  SELECT at.league_id, at.league_name, at.team_id, at.team_long_name, 
         COALESCE(SUM(tw.wins),0) AS total_wins
  FROM all_teams_league at
  LEFT JOIN team_wins tw
    ON at.league_id = tw.league_id AND at.team_id = tw.team_id
  GROUP BY at.league_id, at.team_id
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT *,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY league_id ORDER BY total_wins ASC, team_long_name ASC) AS rn
  FROM total_team_wins
)
SELECT league_id, league_name, team_id, team_long_name, total_wins
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1

WITH first_event AS (

    MIN(stamp) AS first_target_stamp

    a.stamp
  FROM activity_log a
  LEFT JOIN first_event f
    ON a.session = f.session
  WHERE
    TRIM(a.search_type) != ''
    AND (f.first_target_stamp IS NULL OR a.stamp < f.first_target_stamp)
),
pre_click_counts AS (
  SELECT
    session,

  FROM pre_click_events
  GROUP BY session
),
min_count AS (

)
SELECT

  e.path,
  e.search_type
FROM pre_click_events e
JOIN pre_click_counts c ON e.session = c.session
JOIN min_count m ON c.event_count = m.min_event_count
ORDER BY e.session, e.stamp

WITH ordered_logs AS (

)
SELECT
  third_page_url,

ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC, third_page_url
LIMIT 3;

WITH first_purchase AS (
  SELECT 
    c.customer_id,
    MIN(p.payment_date) AS first_payment_date
  FROM customer c
  JOIN payment p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.customer_id
),

  SELECT 
    c.customer_id,
    SUM(p.amount) AS total_ltv
  FROM customer c
  JOIN payment p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
sales_windows AS (
  SELECT 
    fp.customer_id,
    ltv.total_ltv,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(STRFTIME('%s', p.payment_date) AS INTEGER) <= CAST(STRFTIME('%s', fp.first_payment_date) AS INTEGER) + 7*24*60*60 THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) AS sales_7d,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(STRFTIME('%s', p.payment_date) AS INTEGER) <= CAST(STRFTIME('%s', fp.first_payment_date) AS INTEGER) + 30*24*60*60 THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) AS sales_30d
  FROM first_purchase fp
  JOIN payment p ON fp.customer_id = p.customer_id
  JOIN ltv ON ltv.customer_id = fp.customer_id
  GROUP BY fp.customer_id, ltv.total_ltv, fp.first_payment_date
)
SELECT

  AVG(total_ltv) AS avg_total_ltv
FROM sales_windows
WHERE total_ltv > 0;

WITH Entertainer_StyleCounts AS (
  SELECT EntertainerID, COUNT(*) AS style_count
  FROM Entertainer_Styles
  GROUP BY EntertainerID
  HAVING style_count <= 3

Customer_PrefCounts AS (
  SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS pref_count
  FROM Musical_Preferences
  GROUP BY CustomerID
  HAVING pref_count <= 3
),
EntFirstSecond AS (
  SELECT e.EntertainerID, 
         MAX(CASE WHEN es.StyleStrength = 1 THEN es.StyleID END) AS EStyle1,
         MAX(CASE WHEN es.StyleStrength = 2 THEN es.StyleID END) AS EStyle2
  FROM Entertainers e
  JOIN Entertainer_StyleCounts esc ON e.EntertainerID = esc.EntertainerID
  JOIN Entertainer_Styles es ON e.EntertainerID = es.EntertainerID
  GROUP BY e.EntertainerID
),
CustFirstSecond AS (
  SELECT c.CustomerID,
         MAX(CASE WHEN mp.PreferenceSeq = 1 THEN mp.StyleID END) AS CStyle1,
         MAX(CASE WHEN mp.PreferenceSeq = 2 THEN mp.StyleID END) AS CStyle2
  FROM Customers c
  JOIN Customer_PrefCounts cpc ON c.CustomerID = cpc.CustomerID
  JOIN Musical_Preferences mp ON c.CustomerID = mp.CustomerID
  GROUP BY c.CustomerID

SELECT e.EntStageName, c.CustLastName

  ON ( (ef.EStyle1 = cf.CStyle1 AND ef.EStyle2 = cf.CStyle2)
        OR (ef.EStyle1 = cf.CStyle2 AND ef.EStyle2 = cf.CStyle1) )
JOIN Customers c ON cf.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

  JOIN actor_max_films_with_director m

)

```sql
WITH yash_chopra_pid AS (
  SELECT PID
  FROM Person
  WHERE Name = 'Yash Chopra'
),
actor_director_films AS (
  SELECT
    mc.PID AS actor_pid,
    md.PID AS director_pid,
    COUNT(DISTINCT mc.MID) AS films_together
  FROM M_Cast mc
  JOIN M_Director md ON mc.MID = md.MID
  WHERE mc.PID != md.PID
  GROUP BY mc.PID, md.PID
),
actor_max_films_with_director AS (
  SELECT
    actor_pid,
    MAX(films_together) AS max_films
  FROM actor_director_films
  GROUP BY actor_pid
),
actors_more_with_yash_chopra AS (
  SELECT
    a.actor_pid
  FROM actor_director_films a
  JOIN yash_chopra_pid y ON a.director_pid = y.PID
  JOIN actor_max_films_with_director m
    ON a.actor_pid = m.actor_pid AND a.films_together = m.max_films
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_actors
FROM actors_more_with_yash_chopra;
```

WITH delivered_orders AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_city
  FROM olist_orders o
  JOIN olist_customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
),
city_payments AS (
  SELECT d.customer_city,
         SUM(p.payment_value) AS total_payments,
         COUNT(DISTINCT d.order_id) AS order_count
  FROM delivered_orders d
  JOIN olist_order_payments p ON d.order_id = p.order_id
  GROUP BY d.customer_city
),
lowest_five_cities AS (
  SELECT customer_city, total_payments, order_count
  FROM city_payments
  ORDER BY total_payments ASC
  LIMIT 5
)
SELECT
  AVG(total_payments) AS avg_of_lowest_total_payments,
  AVG(order_count) AS avg_of_lowest_total_order_counts
FROM lowest_five_cities;

WITH italian_customers AS (
  SELECT cu.cust_id
  FROM customers cu
  JOIN countries co ON cu.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'Italy'
),

  SELECT s.cust_id,
         SUM(s.amount_sold - s.quantity_sold * c.unit_cost) AS profit
  FROM sales s
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  JOIN costs c ON s.prod_id = c.prod_id AND s.time_id = c.time_id AND s.promo_id = c.promo_id AND s.channel_id = c.channel_id
  WHERE t.calendar_year = 2021 AND t.calendar_month_number = 12
    AND s.cust_id IN (SELECT cust_id FROM italian_customers)
  GROUP BY s.cust_id
),

tiered_profits AS (
  SELECT cust_id, profit,
         NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY profit DESC) AS profit_tier
  FROM december_sales_profits
)
SELECT profit_tier,
       MAX(profit) AS highest_profit,
       MIN(profit) AS lowest_profit
FROM tiered_profits
GROUP BY profit_tier
ORDER BY profit_tier

WITH base_sales AS (
  SELECT
    s.prod_id,
    t.calendar_month_number AS month,
    t.calendar_year AS year,
    s.amount_sold,
    s.channel_id,
    s.promo_id,
    c.country_id,
    co.country_name
  FROM sales s
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'France'
    AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
    AND s.promo_id = 1
    AND s.channel_id = 1
),
pivot_sales AS (
  SELECT
    prod_id,
    month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN amount_sold ELSE 0 END) AS amt_2019,
    SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2020 THEN amount_sold ELSE 0 END) AS amt_2020
  FROM base_sales
  GROUP BY prod_id, month
),
projected_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    prod_id,
    month,
    CASE
      WHEN amt_2019 != 0 THEN (((amt_2020 - amt_2019) / amt_2019) * amt_2020) + amt_2020
      ELSE amt_2020
    END AS projected_amt_2021
  FROM pivot_sales
),
proj_with_currency AS (
  SELECT
    p.prod_id,
    p.month,
    ROUND(
      p.projected_amt_2021 * COALESCE(cur.to_us, 1), 2
    ) AS projected_usd
  FROM projected_2021 p
  LEFT JOIN currency cur ON cur.country = 'France' AND cur.year = 2020 AND cur.month = p.month
),
monthly_avg_usd AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    AVG(projected_usd) AS avg_usd
  FROM proj_with_currency
  GROUP BY month
),
ordered_avg AS (
  SELECT
    avg_usd,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY avg_usd) AS rn,
    COUNT(*) OVER () AS total
  FROM monthly_avg_usd
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_usd) AS median_avg_usd
FROM ordered_avg
WHERE rn = (total + 1) / 2
   OR rn = (total + 2) / 2;

WITH sales_filtered AS (
    SELECT
        s.product_id,
        s.country_id,
        s.channel_total_id,
        s.promo_total_id,
        s.time_id,
        t.year,
        t.month,
        s.amount,
        s.currency_id
    FROM sales s
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    JOIN countries c ON s.country_id = c.country_id
    WHERE 
        c.country_name = 'France'
        AND t.year IN (2019, 2020)
        AND s.promo_total_id = 1
        AND s.channel_total_id = 1
),
sales_pivot AS (
    SELECT
        sf.product_id,
        sf.month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sf.year = 2019 THEN sf.amount ELSE 0 END) AS amount_2019,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sf.year = 2020 THEN sf.amount ELSE 0 END) AS amount_2020,
        s2019.currency_id AS currency_id_2019,
        s2020.currency_id AS currency_id_2020
    FROM sales_filtered sf
    LEFT JOIN sales_filtered s2019
        ON sf.product_id = s2019.product_id AND sf.month = s2019.month AND s2019.year = 2019
    LEFT JOIN sales_filtered s2020
        ON sf.product_id = s2020.product_id AND sf.month = s2020.month AND s2020.year = 2020
    GROUP BY sf.product_id, sf.month
),
projection_raw AS (
    SELECT
        sp.product_id,
        sp.month,
        sp.amount_2019,
        sp.amount_2020,
        sp.currency_id_2020,
        CASE
            WHEN sp.amount_2019 IS NOT NULL AND sp.amount_2019 != 0
            THEN (((sp.amount_2020 - sp.amount_2019) * 1.0) / sp.amount_2019) * sp.amount_2020 + sp.amount_2020
            ELSE sp.amount_2020
        END AS projected_sales_2021
    FROM sales_pivot sp
),
proj_with_currency AS (
    SELECT
        pr.product_id,
        pr.month,
        ROUND(
            pr.projected_sales_2021 *
            COALESCE(cur.rate_to_usd, 1)
        , 2) AS projected_sales_2021_usd
    FROM projection_raw pr
    LEFT JOIN currency cur 
        ON pr.currency_id_2020 = cur.currency_id AND cur.year = 2020 AND cur.month = pr.month
),
monthly_avg_usd AS (
    SELECT
        month,
        AVG(projected_sales_2021_usd) AS avg_projected_sales_2021_usd
    FROM proj_with_currency
    GROUP BY month

WITH director_movies AS (
  SELECT
    dm.name_id AS director_id,
    n.name AS director_name,
    m.id AS movie_id,
    m.duration AS movie_duration,
    m.year AS movie_year,
    r.avg_rating,
    r.total_votes
  FROM director_mapping dm
  JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
  JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
  LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
),
inter_movie_gap AS (
  SELECT
    director_id,
    director_name,
    movie_id,
    movie_duration,
    avg_rating,
    total_votes,
    movie_year,
    movie_year - LAG(movie_year) OVER (PARTITION BY director_id ORDER BY movie_year) AS diff
  FROM director_movies
  WHERE movie_year IS NOT NULL
),
director_stats AS (
  SELECT
    director_id,
    director_name,
    COUNT(movie_id) AS movie_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(movie_duration,0)) AS total_movie_duration,
    ROUND(AVG(avg_rating),2) AS avg_rating,
    SUM(COALESCE(total_votes,0)) AS total_votes,
    MIN(avg_rating) AS min_rating,
    MAX(avg_rating) AS max_rating,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(diff) > 0 THEN ROUND(AVG(diff)) ELSE NULL END AS avg_inter_movie_duration
  FROM inter_movie_gap
  GROUP BY director_id, director_name
)
SELECT
  director_id,
  director_name,
  movie_count,
  avg_inter_movie_duration,
  avg_rating,
  total_votes,
  min_rating,
  max_rating,
  total_movie_duration
FROM director_stats
ORDER BY movie_count DESC, total_movie_duration DESC
LIMIT 9;

WITH filtered_lap_times AS (
  SELECT lt.race_id, lt.driver_id, lt.lap, lt.position
  FROM lap_times lt
  WHERE lt.lap > 1
),
valid_lap_times AS (
  SELECT flt.*
  FROM filtered_lap_times flt
  LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps
    ON flt.race_id = ps.race_id
    AND flt.driver_id = ps.driver_id
    AND flt.lap = ps.lap
  LEFT JOIN retirements r
    ON flt.race_id = r.race_id
    AND flt.driver_id = r.driver_id
    AND flt.lap = r.lap
  WHERE ps.driver_id IS NULL AND r.driver_id IS NULL
),
overtakes AS (
  SELECT
    prev.driver_id AS overtaken_id,
    curr.driver_id AS overtaker_id
  FROM valid_lap_times prev
  JOIN valid_lap_times curr
    ON prev.race_id = curr.race_id
    AND prev.lap = curr.lap
    AND prev.position = curr.position + 1
),
overtaken_count AS (
  SELECT overtaken_id AS driver_id, COUNT(*) AS overtaken_events
  FROM overtakes
  GROUP BY overtaken_id
),
overtaker_count AS (
  SELECT overtaker_id AS driver_id, COUNT(*) AS overtaker_events
  FROM overtakes
  GROUP BY overtaker_id
)
SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS full_name

LEFT JOIN overtaken_count oc ON d.driver_id = oc.driver_id
LEFT JOIN overtaker_count ok ON d.driver_id = ok.driver_id
WHERE IFNULL(oc.overtaken_events, 0) > IFNULL(ok.overtaker_events, 0);

WITH italian_customers AS (
  SELECT c.cust_id
  FROM customers c
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'Italy'
),
dec_2021_profits AS (
  SELECT
    s.cust_id,
    SUM(s.quantity_sold * (p.prod_list_price - p.prod_min_price)) AS total_profit
  FROM sales s
  JOIN italian_customers ic ON s.cust_id = ic.cust_id
  JOIN products p ON s.prod_id = p.prod_id
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  WHERE t.calendar_year = 2021
    AND t.calendar_month_number = 12
  GROUP BY s.cust_id
),
profit_stats AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(total_profit) AS min_profit,
    MAX(total_profit) AS max_profit
  FROM dec_2021_profits
),
bucketed_profits AS (
  SELECT
    d.cust_id,
    d.total_profit,
    CAST(
      1 + (9.0 * (d.total_profit - ps.min_profit) 
           / CASE WHEN ps.max_profit = ps.min_profit THEN 1 ELSE (ps.max_profit - ps.min_profit) END
      ) AS INTEGER
    ) AS profit_bucket
  FROM dec_2021_profits d
  CROSS JOIN profit_stats ps
)
SELECT
  profit_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS num_customers,
  MIN(total_profit) AS min_total_profit,
  MAX(total_profit) AS max_total_profit
FROM bucketed_profits
GROUP BY profit_bucket
ORDER BY profit_bucket

WITH italian_customers AS (
  SELECT c.cust_id
  FROM customers c
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'Italy'
),
dec_2021_profits AS (
  SELECT
    s.cust_id,
    SUM(s.quantity_sold * (p.prod_list_price - p.prod_min_price)) AS total_profit
  FROM sales s
  JOIN italian_customers ic ON s.cust_id = ic.cust_id
  JOIN products p ON s.prod_id = p.prod_id
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  WHERE t.calendar_year = 2021
    AND t.calendar_month_number = 12
  GROUP BY s.cust_id
),
profit_stats AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(total_profit) AS min_profit,
    MAX(total_profit) AS max_profit
  FROM dec_2021_profits
),
bucketed_profits AS (
  SELECT
    d.cust_id,
    d.total_profit,
    CAST(
      1 + (9.0 * (d.total_profit - ps.min_profit) 
           / CASE WHEN ps.max_profit = ps.min_profit THEN 1 ELSE (ps.max_profit - ps.min_profit) END
      ) AS INTEGER
    ) AS profit_bucket
  FROM dec_2021_profits d
  CROSS JOIN profit_stats ps
)
SELECT
  profit_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS num_customers,
  MIN(total_profit) AS min_total_profit,
  MAX(total_profit) AS max_total_profit
FROM bucketed_profits
GROUP BY profit_bucket
ORDER BY profit_bucket

        order_id,
        strftime('%Y', order_delivered_customer_date) AS year,
        strftime('%Y-%m', order_delivered_customer_date) AS year_month

monthly_volumes AS (

    FROM delivered_orders
    WHERE year = (SELECT year FROM min_year)
    GROUP BY year_month
)
SELECT
    MAX(monthly_delivered_orders) AS highest_monthly_delivered_orders
FROM monthly_volumes;

WITH winner_games AS (
  SELECT
    bs.BowlerID,
    b.BowlerFirstName,
    b.BowlerLastName,
    bs.MatchID,
    bs.GameNumber,
    bs.HandiCapScore,
    t.TourneyDate,
    t.TourneyLocation as Location
  FROM Bowler_Scores bs
  JOIN Bowlers b ON bs.BowlerID = b.BowlerID
  JOIN Match_Games mg ON bs.MatchID = mg.MatchID AND bs.GameNumber = mg.GameNumber
  JOIN Tourney_Matches tm ON bs.MatchID = tm.MatchID
  JOIN Tournaments t ON tm.TourneyID = t.TourneyID
  WHERE bs.HandiCapScore <= 190
    AND bs.WonGame = 1
    AND t.TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes', 'Totem Lanes', 'Bolero Lanes')
),
bowlers_with_all_three_venues AS (
  SELECT
    BowlerID
  FROM winner_games
  GROUP BY BowlerID
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT Location) = 3
)
SELECT
  wg.BowlerID,
  wg.BowlerFirstName,
  wg.BowlerLastName,
  wg.MatchID AS MatchNumber,
  wg.GameNumber,
  wg.HandiCapScore,
  wg.TourneyDate,
  wg.Location
FROM winner_games wg
JOIN bowlers_with_all_three_venues b3v ON wg.BowlerID = b3v.BowlerID
ORDER BY wg.BowlerID, wg.TourneyDate, wg.MatchID, wg.GameNumber;

WITH
filtered_sales AS (
  SELECT
    s.prod_id,
    s.time_id,
    t.calendar_month_number AS month,
    t.calendar_year AS year,
    s.amount_sold,
    c.country_name
  FROM sales s
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  JOIN countries c ON s.cust_id = c.country_id
  WHERE
    c.country_name = 'France'
    AND s.promo_id = 1
    AND s.channel_id = 1
    AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
),
monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    prod_id,
    month,
    year,
    SUM(amount_sold) AS total_amount
  FROM filtered_sales
  GROUP BY prod_id, year, month
),
pivoted_sales AS (
  SELECT
    a.prod_id,
    a.month,
    IFNULL(a.total_amount, 0) AS amt_2019,
    IFNULL(b.total_amount, 0) AS amt_2020
  FROM
    (SELECT * FROM monthly_sales WHERE year = 2019) a
    LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM monthly_sales WHERE year = 2020) b
    ON a.prod_id = b.prod_id AND a.month = b.month

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    b.prod_id,
    b.month,
    IFNULL(a.total_amount, 0) AS amt_2019,
    IFNULL(b.total_amount, 0) AS amt_2020
  FROM
    (SELECT * FROM monthly_sales WHERE year = 2020) b
    LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM monthly_sales WHERE year = 2019) a
    ON b.prod_id = a.prod_id AND b.month = a.month
  WHERE a.prod_id IS NULL
),
projected_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    prod_id,
    month,
    amt_2019,
    amt_2020,
    CASE
      WHEN amt_2019 != 0 THEN (((amt_2020 - amt_2019) * 1.0) / amt_2019) * amt_2020 + amt_2020
      ELSE amt_2020
    END AS proj_2021_amt
  FROM pivoted_sales
),
fx AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    to_us
  FROM currency
  WHERE country = 'France' AND year = 2021
),
projected_with_fx AS (
  SELECT
    p.month,
    p.prod_id,
    p.proj_2021_amt,
    IFNULL(f.to_us, 1) AS to_usd,
    ROUND(p.proj_2021_amt * IFNULL(f.to_us, 1), 2) AS proj_2021_usd
  FROM projected_2021 p
  LEFT JOIN fx f ON p.month = f.month
)
SELECT
  month,
  ROUND(AVG(proj_2021_usd), 2) AS avg_projected_2021_usd
FROM projected_with_fx
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

    IFNULL(ms_2020.total_amount, 0) AS amount_2020

Provided benchmark documentation:
## Projection Calculation Method

### Steps for Projection Calculation

1. **Aggregate Historical Sales Data**

   - **Data Collection**: Gather sales data for products sold in France, including sales amounts each month for the years 2019, 2020, and 2021.
   - **Summarize Sales**: Sum up the sales amounts for each product, country, month, and year.

2. **Calculate Average Sales**

   - **Monthly Averages**: Compute the average sales amount for each product and month across all available months to establish a baseline of typical sales.

3. **Project Sales for 2021**

   - **Identify Changes**: Determine how sales changed from 2019 to 2020 for each product and month. Calculate the percentage change in sales from 2019 to 2020.
   - **Apply Changes**: Use this percentage change to estimate the sales for each month in 2021.

   **Projection Formula**:
   - For 2021:
     - Calculate the difference in sales between 2020 and 2019.
     - Compute the percentage change relative to 2019 sales.
     - Apply this percentage change to the 2020 sales to estimate 2021 sales.
     - The formula used in the SQL query is:

       ```plaintext
       (((Sales in 2020 - Sales in 2019) / Sales in 2019) * Sales in 2020) + Sales in 2020
       ```

     - This formula calculates the projected sales for 2021 based on the observed trend from 2019 to 2020.

   - For other years (not 2021):
     - Use the average sales value calculated for each month.

4. **Adjust for Currency Conversion**

   - **Conversion Rates**: Convert the projected sales figures into USD using monthly conversion rates.
   - **Currency Adjustment**: Multiply the projected sales figures by the conversion rates to adjust to USD. If specific rates are not available, use a default rate of 1.

5. **Calculate Monthly Averages in USD**

   - **Monthly Projections**: Compute the average projected sales for each month in 2021, adjusting for currency conversion. Round the results to two decimal places.

6. **Compile Results**

   - **Organize Data**: Arrange the projected sales figures in a report, showing the estimated sales for each month in USD.

### Summary

The projection calculation involves analyzing historical sales data from 2019 and 2020 to determine trends, applying these trends to estimate sales for 2021, and adjusting for currency differences. The result is a forecast of monthly sales in USD for 2021.

WITH cleaned_prices AS (
    SELECT
        market_date AS date,
        ticker,
        CASE
            WHEN volume = '-' THEN 0.0
            WHEN volume LIKE '%K' THEN CAST(REPLACE(volume, 'K', '') AS FLOAT) * 1000
            WHEN volume LIKE '%M' THEN CAST(REPLACE(volume, 'M', '') AS FLOAT) * 1000000
            ELSE CAST(volume AS FLOAT)
        END AS clean_volume
    FROM bitcoin_prices
    WHERE market_date BETWEEN '2021-08-01' AND '2021-08-10'
),
ranked_prices AS (
    SELECT
        date,
        ticker,
        clean_volume,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ticker, date ORDER BY date) AS rn
    FROM cleaned_prices
),
nonzero_volumes AS (
    SELECT
        date,
        ticker,
        clean_volume,
        LAG(date) OVER (PARTITION BY ticker ORDER BY date) AS prev_date,
        LAG(clean_volume) OVER (PARTITION BY ticker ORDER BY date) AS prev_volume
    FROM (
        SELECT * FROM ranked_prices WHERE clean_volume > 0
    )
),
full_daily_changes AS (
    SELECT
        cp.date,
        cp.ticker,
        cp.clean_volume,
        (
            SELECT nzv_prev.clean_volume
            FROM nonzero_volumes nzv_prev
            WHERE nzv_prev.ticker = cp.ticker AND nzv_prev.date < cp.date
            ORDER BY nzv_prev.date DESC
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS prev_nonzero_volume
    FROM cleaned_prices cp
)
SELECT
    date,
    ticker,
    clean_volume AS volume,
    prev_nonzero_volume,
    CASE
        WHEN prev_nonzero_volume IS NOT NULL AND prev_nonzero_volume != 0
            THEN ROUND((clean_volume - prev_nonzero_volume) / prev_nonzero_volume * 100, 4)
        ELSE NULL
    END AS pct_change
FROM full_daily_changes
ORDER BY ticker, date;

```sql
WITH cleaned_prices AS (
    SELECT
        date,
        ticker,
        -- Handle '-' as 0, strip K/M and convert to numeric, else cast as float
        CASE
            WHEN volume = '-' THEN 0.0
            WHEN volume LIKE '%K' THEN CAST(REPLACE(volume, 'K', '') AS FLOAT) * 1000
            WHEN volume LIKE '%M' THEN CAST(REPLACE(volume, 'M', '') AS FLOAT) * 1000000
            ELSE CAST(volume AS FLOAT)
        END AS clean_volume
    FROM bitcoin_prices
    WHERE date BETWEEN '2021-08-01' AND '2021-08-10'
),
indexed_volumes AS (
    SELECT
        date,
        ticker,
        clean_volume,
        -- Only non-zero volumes are used to determine previous day's volume
        LAG(clean_volume) OVER (
            PARTITION BY ticker
            ORDER BY date
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
        ) AS prev_clean_volume
    FROM (
        SELECT
            date,
            ticker,
            clean_volume
        FROM cleaned_prices
        WHERE clean_volume > 0
    )
),
final_changes AS (
    SELECT
        cp.date,
        cp.ticker,
        cp.clean_volume AS volume,
        -- Find the most recent non-zero previous volume for this ticker < this date
        (
            SELECT iv.clean_volume
            FROM indexed_volumes iv
            WHERE iv.ticker = cp.ticker
              AND iv.date < cp.date
            ORDER BY iv.date DESC
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS prev_nonzero_volume
    FROM cleaned_prices cp
)
SELECT
    date,
    ticker,
    volume,
    prev_nonzero_volume,
    CASE
        WHEN prev_nonzero_volume IS NULL OR prev_nonzero_volume = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND((volume - prev_nonzero_volume) / prev_nonzero_volume * 100, 4)
    END AS pct_change
FROM final_changes
WHERE date BETWEEN '2021-08-01' AND '2021-08-10'
ORDER BY ticker, date;

WITH CleanedSalary AS (
    SELECT 
        CompanyName,
        Location,
        CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(Salary, '$', ''), ',', ''), '₹', ''), ' ', '') AS FLOAT) AS Salary_numeric
    FROM SalaryDataset
    WHERE Location IN ('Mumbai', 'Pune', 'New Delhi', 'Hyderabad')
          AND Salary IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(Salary) != ''
),
AverageSalaryByCompanyLocation AS (
    SELECT 
        Location,
        CompanyName,
        AVG(Salary_numeric) AS AvgSalaryInState
    FROM CleanedSalary
    GROUP BY Location, CompanyName
),
Top5CompaniesEachLocation AS (
    SELECT 
        Location,
        CompanyName,
        AvgSalaryInState,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Location ORDER BY AvgSalaryInState DESC) AS rn
    FROM AverageSalaryByCompanyLocation
),
NationalAverageByCompany AS (
    SELECT 
        CompanyName,
        AVG(Salary_numeric) AS AvgSalaryInCountry
    FROM CleanedSalary
    GROUP BY CompanyName
)
SELECT 
    t.Location,
    t.CompanyName,
    t.AvgSalaryInState,
    n.AvgSalaryInCountry
FROM Top5CompaniesEachLocation t
JOIN NationalAverageByCompany n 
    ON t.CompanyName = n.CompanyName
WHERE t.rn <= 5
ORDER BY t.Location, t.AvgSalaryInState DESC
