Using a Salary Dataset where the salary values need to be cleaned by removing non-numeric characters and converting them to a numeric type, write a detailed SQL query that identifies the top 5 companies by average salary in each of Mumbai, Pune, New Delhi, and Hyderabad, then compares each company’s average salary in those cities to the overall national average salary. The final result should display four columns: Location, Company Name, Average Salary in State, and Average Salary in Country, listing only the top 5 companies in each of the specified locations.
Return your final answer as exactly one fenced ```sql block containing the single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query that answers the question. Do not include exploratory SQL in the final answer. Use the supplied documentation; no user simulator is available.

    FROM SalaryDataset
    WHERE Location IN ('Mumbai', 'Pune', 'New Delhi', 'Hyderabad')
          AND Salary IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(Salary) != ''
),
AverageSalaryByCompanyLocation AS (

Top5CompaniesEachLocation AS (

NationalAverageByCompany AS (

```sql
WITH BestSellingArtist AS (
    SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS total_sales
    FROM artists ar
    JOIN albums al ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
    JOIN tracks t ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
    JOIN invoice_items ii ON t.TrackId = ii.TrackId
    GROUP BY ar.ArtistId
    ORDER BY total_sales DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
RelevantAlbums AS (
    SELECT al.AlbumId
    FROM albums al
    JOIN BestSellingArtist bsa ON al.ArtistId = bsa.ArtistId
),
CustomerSpending AS (
    SELECT c.FirstName, SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS spent
    FROM customers c
    JOIN invoices i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
    JOIN invoice_items ii ON i.InvoiceId = ii.InvoiceId
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    WHERE t.AlbumId IN (SELECT AlbumId FROM RelevantAlbums)
    GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName
)
SELECT FirstName, spent
FROM CustomerSpending
WHERE spent < 1
ORDER BY FirstName;
```

```sql
WITH step_scores AS (

        m.version AS model_version,
        m.L1_model,
        m.step,

    FROM model m
    JOIN model_score ms ON m.name = ms.name AND m.version = ms.version AND m.step = ms.step
),
stack_scores AS (
    SELECT
        model_name,
        model_version,
        step,
        test_score AS stack_test_score
    FROM step_scores
    WHERE L2_model = 'Stack'
),
non_stack_max_scores AS (
    SELECT
        model_name,
        model_version,
        step,
        MAX(test_score) AS max_non_stack_score
    FROM step_scores
    WHERE L2_model <> 'Stack'
    GROUP BY model_name, model_version, step
),
status_by_model AS (
    SELECT
        ns.model_name,
        ns.model_version,
        ns.step,
        CASE
            WHEN ns.max_non_stack_score < ss.stack_test_score THEN 'strong'
            WHEN ns.max_non_stack_score = ss.stack_test_score THEN 'soft'
            ELSE NULL
        END AS status
    FROM non_stack_max_scores ns
    JOIN stack_scores ss
      ON ns.model_name = ss.model_name AND ns.model_version = ss.model_version AND ns.step = ss.step
),
model_primary_status AS (
    SELECT
        model_name,
        model_version,
        MAX(CASE status WHEN 'strong' THEN 2 WHEN 'soft' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS status_score
    FROM status_by_model
    GROUP BY model_name, model_version
),
model_status_label AS (
    SELECT
        model_name,
        model_version,
        CASE status_score WHEN 2 THEN 'strong' WHEN 1 THEN 'soft' ELSE NULL END AS status
    FROM model_primary_status
    WHERE status_score > 0
),
model_l1_status AS (

        m.model_name,
        m.model_version,
        m.L1_model,
        s.status
    FROM (
        SELECT name AS model_name, version AS model_version, L1_model FROM model
    ) m
    JOIN model_status_label s ON m.model_name = s.model_name AND m.model_version = s.model_version
),
l1_status_counts AS (
    SELECT
        L1_model,
        status,
        COUNT(*) AS occurrences
    FROM model_l1_status
    GROUP BY L1_model, status
),
ranked_l1 AS (
    SELECT
        l1_status_counts.status,

    FROM l1_status_counts
)

    L1_model,
    occurrences
FROM ranked_l1
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY status, L1_model
```

WITH step_scores AS (

```sql
        ms.L1_model,

    FROM model m

),
stack_scores AS (
    SELECT
        model_name,
        model_version,
        step,
        test_score AS stack_test_score
    FROM step_scores
    WHERE L2_model = 'Stack'
),
non_stack_max_scores AS (
    SELECT
        model_name,
        model_version,
        step,
        MAX(test_score) AS max_non_stack_score
    FROM step_scores
    WHERE L2_model <> 'Stack'
    GROUP BY model_name, model_version, step
),
status_by_model AS (
    SELECT
        ns.model_name,
        ns.model_version,
        CASE
            WHEN ns.max_non_stack_score < ss.stack_test_score THEN 'strong'
            WHEN ns.max_non_stack_score = ss.stack_test_score THEN 'soft'
            ELSE NULL
        END AS status,
        max(ss.stack_test_score) AS stack_test_score
    FROM non_stack_max_scores ns
    JOIN stack_scores ss
      ON ns.model_name = ss.model_name AND ns.model_version = ss.model_version AND ns.step = ss.step
    GROUP BY ns.model_name, ns.model_version, ns.max_non_stack_score, ss.stack_test_score
),
model_primary_status AS (
    -- In case a model has both statuses in different steps, take 'strong' over 'soft'
    SELECT
        model_name,
        model_version,
        CASE
            WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'strong' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'strong'
            WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'soft' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'soft'
        END AS primary_status
    FROM status_by_model
    WHERE status IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY model_name, model_version
),
model_l1_association AS (
    SELECT
        m.name AS model_name,
        m.version AS model_version,
        ml1.L1_model,
        mps.primary_status
    FROM model m
    JOIN (
        SELECT model_id, L1_model
        FROM model_score
        GROUP BY model_id, L1_model
    ) ml1 ON m.id = ml1.model_id
    JOIN model_primary_status mps
      ON m.name = mps.model_name AND m.version = mps.model_version
    WHERE mps.primary_status IN ('strong', 'soft')
),
l1_status_counts AS (
    SELECT
        L1_model,
        primary_status AS status,
        COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM model_l1_association
    GROUP BY L1_model, primary_status
),
status_max_l1 AS (
    SELECT
        status,
        L1_model,
        cnt,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY status ORDER BY cnt DESC) AS rnk
    FROM l1_status_counts
)
SELECT
    status,
    L1_model,
    cnt AS num_occurrences
FROM status_max_l1
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY status, L1_model
;
```

```sql
WITH motorcycle_parties AS (
  SELECT
    case_id,
    party_number,
    -- Determining helmet usage: Assume 'Helmet' or codes containing 'Helmet' denote helmet use
    CASE
      WHEN (party_safety_equipment_1 LIKE '%Helmet%' OR party_safety_equipment_2 LIKE '%Helmet%') THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS helmet_used
  FROM parties
  WHERE statewide_vehicle_type LIKE '%Motorcycle%'
),
collision_helmet_groups AS (
  SELECT
    case_id,
    MAX(helmet_used) as any_helmet_used,
    MIN(helmet_used) as all_helmet_used
  FROM motorcycle_parties
  GROUP BY case_id
),
motorcycle_victim_fatalities AS (
  SELECT
    v.case_id,
    v.party_number
  FROM victims v
  JOIN parties p
    ON v.case_id = p.case_id AND v.party_number = p.party_number
  WHERE p.statewide_vehicle_type LIKE '%Motorcycle%'
    AND v.victim_degree_of_injury = 'Killed'
),
fatalities_by_helmet AS (
  SELECT
    chg.any_helmet_used AS helmet_used,
    COUNT(DISTINCT mvf.id) AS fatalities,
    COUNT(DISTINCT chg.case_id) AS total_collisions
  FROM collision_helmet_groups chg
  LEFT JOIN motorcycle_victim_fatalities mvf
    ON chg.case_id = mvf.case_id
  GROUP BY helmet_used
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN helmet_used = 1 THEN 'Helmet used in collision' ELSE 'No helmet used in collision' END as helmet_group,
  COALESCE(CAST(fatalities AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(total_collisions, 0) * 100, 0) as fatality_rate_percent
FROM fatalities_by_helmet
ORDER BY helmet_used DESC;
```

```sql
    FROM rental r
    JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id

)
SELECT

FROM cust_with_top_actor_rental cwtar
```

```sql
WITH races_50s AS (
  SELECT race_id, year, round
  FROM races
  WHERE year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1959
),
driver_50s_races AS (
  SELECT 
    res.driver_id, 
    d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_name, 
    r.year, 
    res.race_id, 
    res.constructor_id, 
    r.round
  FROM results res
  JOIN races_50s r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
  JOIN drivers d ON res.driver_id = d.driver_id
),
driver_year_rounds AS (
  SELECT
    driver_id,
    driver_name,
    year,
    MIN(round) AS first_round,
    MAX(round) AS last_round,
    COUNT(DISTINCT round) AS n_rounds
  FROM driver_50s_races
  GROUP BY driver_id, driver_name, year
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT round) >= 2
),
driver_year_first_last_constructors AS (
  SELECT
    dyr.driver_id,
    dyr.driver_name,
    dyr.year,
    MIN(fr.constructor_id) AS first_constructor_id,
    MIN(lr.constructor_id) AS last_constructor_id
  FROM driver_year_rounds dyr
  JOIN driver_50s_races fr ON fr.driver_id = dyr.driver_id AND fr.year = dyr.year AND fr.round = dyr.first_round
  JOIN driver_50s_races lr ON lr.driver_id = dyr.driver_id AND lr.year = dyr.year AND lr.round = dyr.last_round
  GROUP BY dyr.driver_id, dyr.driver_name, dyr.year
  HAVING first_constructor_id = last_constructor_id
)
SELECT DISTINCT driver_name
FROM driver_year_first_last_constructors
ORDER BY driver_name;
```

```sql
WITH driver_race_team AS (
    SELECT
        res.driver_id,
        r.year,
        r.round,
        r.race_id,
        res.constructor_id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY res.driver_id, r.year ORDER BY r.round) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY res.driver_id, r.year) AS num_entries
    FROM results res
    JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
),
all_driver_seasons AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT driver_id, year
    FROM results
    JOIN races ON results.race_id = races.race_id
),
race_list AS (
    SELECT r.race_id, r.year, r.round FROM races r
),
missed_races AS (
    SELECT
        ads.driver_id,
        ads.year,
        rl.round
    FROM all_driver_seasons ads
    JOIN race_list rl ON rl.year = ads.year
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT driver_id, year, round FROM driver_race_team
    ) drt ON drt.driver_id = ads.driver_id AND drt.year = ads.year AND drt.round = rl.round
    WHERE drt.round IS NULL
),
grouped_missed AS (
    SELECT
        driver_id,
        year,
        round,
        round - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY driver_id, year ORDER BY round) AS grp
    FROM missed_races
),
missed_ranges AS (
    SELECT
        driver_id,
        year,
        MIN(round) AS first_missed_round,
        MAX(round) AS last_missed_round,
        COUNT(*) AS num_missed
    FROM grouped_missed
    GROUP BY driver_id, year, grp
),
filtered_ranges AS (
    SELECT * FROM missed_ranges
    WHERE num_missed < 3
),
before_after_team_switches AS (
    SELECT
        fr.*,
        (SELECT constructor_id FROM driver_race_team drt WHERE drt.driver_id = fr.driver_id AND drt.year = fr.year AND drt.round = fr.first_missed_round - 1 ORDER BY drt.round DESC LIMIT 1) AS before_constructor,
        (SELECT constructor_id FROM driver_race_team drt WHERE drt.driver_id = fr.driver_id AND drt.year = fr.year AND drt.round = fr.last_missed_round + 1 ORDER BY drt.round ASC LIMIT 1) AS after_constructor
    FROM filtered_ranges fr
),
team_switch_hiatuses AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM before_after_team_switches
    WHERE before_constructor IS NOT NULL
      AND after_constructor IS NOT NULL
      AND before_constructor <> after_constructor
)
SELECT
    AVG(first_missed_round * 1.0) AS avg_first_missed_round,
    AVG(last_missed_round * 1.0) AS avg_last_missed_round
FROM team_switch_hiatuses;
```

```sql
WITH orderlines_ordered AS (
  SELECT
    ol.id AS orderline_id,
    ol.product_id,
    ol.qty as qty_needed,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY ol.id) AS rn,
    SUM(ol.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY ol.id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_qty_needed
  FROM orderlines ol
  WHERE ol.order_id = 423
),
stock_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    s.id as stock_id,
    s.product_id,
    s.qty as stock_qty,
    s.location_id,
    s.purchased,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.product_id ORDER BY s.purchased, s.qty) AS stock_rn
  FROM stock s
  WHERE s.warehouse_id = 1 AND s.qty > 0
),
locations_info AS (
  SELECT
    l.id AS location_id,
    l.aisle,
    l.position
  FROM locations l
),
orderlines_expanded AS (
  -- For each orderline-product, join available stock rows for that product, in purchased order
  SELECT
    o.orderline_id,
    o.product_id,
    o.rn AS orderline_rn,
    o.cumulative_qty_needed,
    o.qty_needed,
    sr.stock_id,
    sr.location_id,
    sr.stock_qty,
    sr.purchased,
    SUM(sr.stock_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY o.product_id ORDER BY sr.purchased, sr.stock_qty ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_stock_available
  FROM orderlines_ordered o
  JOIN stock_ranked sr
    ON o.product_id = sr.product_id
  WHERE 1=1
),
eligible_picks AS (
  -- Only take the stock rows sufficient for cumulative quantity needed for that line (but not after cumulative consumption)
  SELECT
    oe.*,
    l.aisle,
    l.position,
    CASE
      WHEN oe.cumulative_stock_available - oe.stock_qty >= oe.cumulative_qty_needed THEN 0 -- Stock picked in earlier order lines, done
      ELSE
        /* How much needs to be picked from this bin? */
        MIN(
          oe.qty_needed, -- never pick more than required by this line
          -- Maximum needed from this bin to cover cumulative (may be partial)

    END AS pick_qty_calc
  FROM orderlines_expanded oe
  LEFT JOIN locations_info l ON l.location_id = oe.location_id
)
SELECT
  e.orderline_id,
  e.product_id,
  e.stock_id,
  e.aisle,
  e.position,
  MIN(e.pick_qty_calc, e.stock_qty, e.qty_needed) AS pick_qty
FROM eligible_picks e
WHERE e.pick_qty_calc > 0
GROUP BY e.orderline_id, e.product_id, e.stock_id, e.aisle, e.position
HAVING pick_qty > 0
ORDER BY e.orderline_id, e.product_id, e.purchased, e.stock_qty;
```

```sql
WITH cohorts AS (
  SELECT
    l.id AS legislator_id,
    l.gender,
    lt.state,
    DATE(MIN(lt.term_start)) AS first_term_start
  FROM legislators l
  JOIN legislators_terms lt ON l.id = lt.legislator_id

),
intervals AS (
  SELECT 0 AS years UNION ALL
  SELECT 2 UNION ALL
  SELECT 4 UNION ALL
  SELECT 6 UNION ALL
  SELECT 8 UNION ALL
  SELECT 10
),
cohort_intervals AS (
  SELECT
    c.legislator_id,
    c.gender,
    c.state,
    c.first_term_start,
    i.years,
    DATE(c.first_term_start, '+' || i.years || ' years') AS interval_date
  FROM cohorts c
  CROSS JOIN intervals i
),
serving_on_date AS (
  SELECT
    ci.legislator_id,
    ci.gender,
    ci.state,
    ci.years,
    CASE
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
        WHERE lt.legislator_id = ci.legislator_id
          AND lt.state = ci.state
          AND lt.term_start <= DATE(ci.interval_date, '-1 day')
          AND lt.term_end > DATE(ci.interval_date, '-1 day')
      ) THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS is_retained
  FROM cohort_intervals ci
),
retention_rates AS (
  SELECT
    s.state,
    s.gender,
    s.years,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN s.is_retained = 1 THEN 1 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS retention_rate
  FROM serving_on_date s
  GROUP BY s.state, s.gender, s.years
),
state_gender_meet_criteria AS (
  SELECT
    r.state
  FROM retention_rates r
  WHERE r.retention_rate > 0
  GROUP BY r.state, r.gender
  HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN r.retention_rate > 0 THEN 1 END) = 6
),
states_with_both_genders AS (
  SELECT
    s.state
  FROM state_gender_meet_criteria s
  JOIN (
    SELECT state FROM retention_rates WHERE gender = 'male'
    GROUP BY state
    HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN retention_rate > 0 THEN 1 END) = 6
  ) m ON s.state = m.state
  JOIN (
    SELECT state FROM retention_rates WHERE gender = 'female'
    GROUP BY state
    HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN retention_rate > 0 THEN 1 END) = 6
  ) f ON s.state = f.state
)
SELECT DISTINCT state AS state_abbreviation
FROM states_with_both_genders
ORDER BY state_abbreviation;
```

```sql
WITH over_runs AS (
    SELECT
        b.match_id,
        b.innings_no,
        b.over_id,
        b.bowler,
        SUM(bs.runs_scored) + IFNULL(SUM(er.extra_runs),0) AS total_runs
    FROM
        ball_by_ball b
        LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs ON b.match_id = bs.match_id AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no AND b.over_id = bs.over_id AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
        LEFT JOIN extra_runs er ON b.match_id = er.match_id AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no AND b.over_id = er.over_id AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
    GROUP BY
        b.match_id, b.innings_no, b.over_id, b.bowler
),
```

```sql
    o.pizza_id,

      WHEN pizza_name = 'Vegetarian' THEN 10
      ELSE 0
    END AS price
  FROM pizza_names
),
extras_count AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    -- Each topping in pizza_get_extras for a given order counts as one extra
    COUNT(topping_id) AS num_extras
  FROM pizza_get_extras
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
  SUM(pp.price + COALESCE(ec.num_extras, 0)) AS total_income
FROM valid_orders vo
JOIN pizza_prices pp ON vo.pizza_id = pp.pizza_id
LEFT JOIN extras_count ec ON vo.order_id = ec.order_id;
```

calls.content:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE
-- Get the initial inventory at December 2018 end per product
initial_stock AS (
  SELECT
    s.product_id,
    s.quantity AS start_inventory,
    pm.minimum_quantity
  FROM stock s
  JOIN product_minimums pm ON s.product_id = pm.product_id
  WHERE s.year = 2018 AND s.month = 12
),
-- Aggregate all order and purchase changes for 2019 by product and month
movements_2019 AS (
  SELECT
    o.product_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS year_month,
    -SUM(ol.quantity) AS movement -- orders decrease inventory
  FROM orders o
  JOIN orderlines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.order_date) = '2019'
  GROUP BY o.product_id, year_month

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    p.product_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', p.purchase_date) AS year_month,
    SUM(p.quantity) AS movement -- purchases increase inventory
  FROM purchases p
  WHERE strftime('%Y', p.purchase_date) = '2019'
  GROUP BY p.product_id, year_month
),
-- Sum movements by product and month
monthly_movements AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    year_month,
    SUM(movement) AS net_movement
  FROM movements_2019
  GROUP BY product_id, year_month
),
-- List each month in 2019
months_2019 AS (
  SELECT '2019-01' AS year_month UNION ALL SELECT '2019-02' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-03' UNION ALL SELECT '2019-04' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-05' UNION ALL SELECT '2019-06' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-07' UNION ALL SELECT '2019-08' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-09' UNION ALL SELECT '2019-10' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-11' UNION ALL SELECT '2019-12'
),
-- Recursively calculate month-by-month inventory and restock if below minimum
recursive_stock AS (
  -- Anchor: January
  SELECT
    i.product_id,
    m.year_month,
    i.start_inventory +
      COALESCE(mm.net_movement, 0) AS ending_inventory,
    i.minimum_quantity
  FROM initial_stock i
  JOIN months_2019 m ON m.year_month = '2019-01'
  LEFT JOIN monthly_movements mm ON mm.product_id = i.product_id AND mm.year_month = m.year_month

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    rs.product_id,
    m.year_month,
    -- Apply inventory movements and restock if below minimum
    CASE
      WHEN prev_end < rs.minimum_quantity THEN
        rs.minimum_quantity + COALESCE(mm.net_movement, 0)
      ELSE
        prev_end + COALESCE(mm.net_movement, 0)
    END AS ending_inventory,
    rs.minimum_quantity
  FROM recursive_stock rs
  JOIN months_2019 m ON m.year_month = 
    CASE
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-01' THEN '2019-02'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-02' THEN '2019-03'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-03' THEN '2019-04'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-04' THEN '2019-05'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-05' THEN '2019-06'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-06' THEN '2019-07'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-07' THEN '2019-08'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-08' THEN '2019-09'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-09' THEN '2019-10'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-10' THEN '2019-11'
      WHEN rs.year_month = '2019-11' THEN '2019-12'
      ELSE NULL END
  LEFT JOIN monthly_movements mm ON mm.product_id = rs.product_id AND mm.year_month = m.year_month
  -- previous period's ending_inventory may get restocked if below min (recursive carry-over)
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT ending_inventory AS prev_end
    FROM recursive_stock prev
    WHERE prev.product_id = rs.product_id AND prev.year_month = rs.year_month
  )
  WHERE rs.year_month <> '2019-12'
),
-- Compute absolute difference between ending_inventory and minimum
abs_diff AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    year_month,
    ending_inventory,
    minimum_quantity,
    ABS(ending_inventory - minimum_quantity) AS abs_difference
  FROM recursive_stock
)
-- Choose month in 2019 of minimal abs difference for each product
SELECT
  product_id,
  year_month,
  abs_difference
FROM (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    year_month,
    abs_difference,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY abs_difference ASC, year_month ASC) AS rn
  FROM abs_diff
)
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY product_id;
```

```sql
FROM sales_per_year s
```

```sql
WITH cn_cities_july AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    date(insert_date) AS dt,
    city_name
  FROM cities
  WHERE country_code_2 = 'cn'
    AND insert_date >= '2021-07-01' AND insert_date < '2021-08-01'
),
ranked_dates AS (
  SELECT
    dt,
    city_name,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY dt) AS rn,
    JULIANDAY(dt) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY dt) AS grp
  FROM cn_cities_july
),
streaks AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(dt) AS start_date,
    MAX(dt) AS end_date,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_len,
    grp
  FROM ranked_dates
  GROUP BY grp
),
min_streak AS (
  SELECT streak_len FROM streaks WHERE streak_len = (SELECT MIN(streak_len) FROM streaks)
  LIMIT 1
),
max_streak AS (
  SELECT streak_len FROM streaks WHERE streak_len = (SELECT MAX(streak_len) FROM streaks)
  LIMIT 1
),
min_max_streaks AS (
  SELECT streak_len FROM min_streak
  UNION ALL
  SELECT streak_len FROM max_streak
),
dates_in_streaks AS (
  SELECT rd.dt, rd.city_name, s.streak_len
  FROM ranked_dates rd
  JOIN streaks s
    ON JULIANDAY(rd.dt) - rd.rn = s.grp
  WHERE s.streak_len IN (SELECT streak_len FROM min_max_streaks)
),
city_formatted AS (
```

```sql
WITH season5_matches AS (
    SELECT match_id
    FROM match
    WHERE season_id = 5
),
player_runs AS (
    SELECT
        bs.match_id,
        bs.innings_no,
        bs.over_id,
        bs.ball_id,
        bs.runs_scored,
        pm.player_id
    FROM batsman_scored bs
    JOIN season5_matches sm ON bs.match_id = sm.match_id
    JOIN player_match pm ON bs.match_id = pm.match_id
        AND pm.player_id = (SELECT p.player_id FROM player p WHERE p.player_id = pm.player_id)
),
agg_player_runs AS (
    SELECT 
        player_id,
        SUM(runs_scored) AS total_runs,
        COUNT(DISTINCT match_id) AS matches_played
    FROM player_runs
    GROUP BY player_id
),
player_batting_avg AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        total_runs * 1.0 / matches_played AS batting_average
    FROM agg_player_runs
    WHERE matches_played > 0
)
SELECT
    p.player_name,
    ROUND(pba.batting_average, 2) AS batting_average
FROM player_batting_avg pba
JOIN player p ON pba.player_id = p.player_id
ORDER BY pba.batting_average DESC
```

```sql
WITH incident_counts AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y', collision_date) AS year,
    pcf_violation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS incident_count
  FROM collisions
  WHERE strftime('%Y', collision_date) IN ('2011', '2021')

),
year_totals AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    SUM(incident_count) AS total_incidents
  FROM incident_counts
  GROUP BY year
),
category_shares AS (
  SELECT
    ic.year,
    ic.pcf_violation_category,
    ic.incident_count,
    yt.total_incidents,
    100.0 * ic.incident_count / yt.total_incidents AS share_percent
  FROM incident_counts ic
  JOIN year_totals yt ON ic.year = yt.year
),
most_common_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    pcf_violation_category
  FROM category_shares
  WHERE year = '2021'

  WHERE cs.year IN ('2011', '2021')
  ORDER BY cs.year
)
SELECT
  (SELECT share_percent FROM shares_2011_2021 WHERE year = '2021') -
```

WITH incident_counts AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y', collision_date) AS year,
    pcf_violation_category,
    COUNT(*) AS incident_count
  FROM collisions
  WHERE strftime('%Y', collision_date) IN ('2011', '2021')
  GROUP BY year, pcf_violation_category
),
year_totals AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    SUM(incident_count) AS total_incidents
  FROM incident_counts
  GROUP BY year
),
category_shares AS (
  SELECT
    ic.year,
    ic.pcf_violation_category,
    ic.incident_count,
    yt.total_incidents,
    100.0 * ic.incident_count / yt.total_incidents AS share_percent
  FROM incident_counts ic
  JOIN year_totals yt ON ic.year = yt.year
),
most_common_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    pcf_violation_category
  FROM category_shares
  WHERE year = '2021'
  ORDER BY share_percent DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
shares_2011_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    cs.year,
    cs.share_percent
  FROM category_shares cs
  JOIN most_common_2021 mc ON cs.pcf_violation_category = mc.pcf_violation_category
  WHERE cs.year IN ('2011', '2021')
  ORDER BY cs.year
)
SELECT
  (SELECT share_percent FROM shares_2011_2021 WHERE year = '2021') -
  (SELECT share_percent FROM shares_2011_2021 WHERE year = '2011') AS percentage_point_change
;

```sql
WITH first_payment_per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    MIN(payment_date) AS first_payment_date
  FROM payment
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
first_rental_info AS (
  SELECT
    fp.customer_id,
    r.rental_id,
    r.inventory_id,
    fp.first_payment_date
  FROM first_payment_per_customer fp
  JOIN rental r ON r.customer_id = fp.customer_id
  JOIN payment p ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id AND p.customer_id = fp.customer_id 
  WHERE p.payment_date = fp.first_payment_date
),

  SELECT
    fri.customer_id,
    f.rating
  FROM first_rental_info fri
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = fri.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
),
customer_total_spend_and_rentals AS (
  SELECT
    p.customer_id,
    SUM(p.amount) AS total_spent,
    COUNT(DISTINCT r.rental_id) AS total_rentals
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  GROUP BY p.customer_id
)
SELECT
  fmr.rating,
  AVG(ctsr.total_spent) AS avg_total_amount_spent_per_customer,
  AVG(ctsr.total_rentals - 1) AS avg_subsequent_rentals_per_customer
FROM first_movie_ratings fmr
JOIN customer_total_spend_and_rentals ctsr ON ctsr.customer_id = fmr.customer_id
GROUP BY fmr.rating
ORDER BY fmr.rating;
```

```sql
WITH ordered_txns AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id, 
    DATE(txn_date) AS txn_date, 
    txn_type, 
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
signed_txns AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id, 
    txn_date, 
    CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END AS amount
  FROM ordered_txns
),
daily_txns AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id, 
    txn_date, 
    SUM(amount) AS daily_net
  FROM signed_txns
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
all_days AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, txn_date FROM daily_txns
  UNION
  SELECT customer_id, DATE(min_date, '+' || seq || ' day') AS txn_date
  FROM (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(txn_date) AS min_date, MAX(txn_date) AS max_date FROM daily_txns GROUP BY customer_id
  ) b
  JOIN (
    SELECT 0 seq UNION SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5 UNION SELECT 6 UNION SELECT 7 UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9
    UNION SELECT 10 UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12 UNION SELECT 13 UNION SELECT 14 UNION SELECT 15 UNION SELECT 16 UNION SELECT 17 UNION SELECT 18 UNION SELECT 19
    UNION SELECT 20 UNION SELECT 21 UNION SELECT 22 UNION SELECT 23 UNION SELECT 24 UNION SELECT 25 UNION SELECT 26 UNION SELECT 27 UNION SELECT 28 UNION SELECT 29
    UNION SELECT 30 UNION SELECT 31 UNION SELECT 32 UNION SELECT 33 UNION SELECT 34 UNION SELECT 35 UNION SELECT 36 UNION SELECT 37 UNION SELECT 38 UNION SELECT 39
    UNION SELECT 40 UNION SELECT 41 UNION SELECT 42 UNION SELECT 43 UNION SELECT 44 UNION SELECT 45 UNION SELECT 46 UNION SELECT 47 UNION SELECT 48 UNION SELECT 49
  ) s
  WHERE DATE(min_date, '+' || seq || ' day') <= max_date
),
daily_balance AS (
  SELECT
    d.customer_id,
    d.txn_date,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(d2.daily_net)
      FROM daily_txns d2
      WHERE d2.customer_id = d.customer_id AND d2.txn_date <= d.txn_date
    ), 0) AS running_balance
  FROM all_days d
),
windowed_balance AS (
  SELECT
    b1.customer_id,
    b1.txn_date,
    (
      SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN running_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE running_balance END)
      FROM daily_balance b2
      WHERE b2.customer_id = b1.customer_id
        AND b2.txn_date <= b1.txn_date
        AND b2.txn_date > DATE(b1.txn_date, '-30 days')
```

```sql
WITH monthly_cities AS (
  SELECT
    STRFTIME('%Y', insert_date) AS year,
    STRFTIME('%m', insert_date) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS cities_added
  FROM cities
  WHERE STRFTIME('%m', insert_date) IN ('04', '05', '06')
    AND STRFTIME('%Y', insert_date) IN ('2021','2022','2023')
  GROUP BY year, month
),
running_totals AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    year,
    cities_added,
    SUM(cities_added) OVER (
      PARTITION BY month ORDER BY year
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS running_total
  FROM monthly_cities
),
growth_calc AS (
  SELECT
    rt.year,
    rt.month,
    rt.cities_added,
    rt.running_total,
    LAG(rt.cities_added) OVER (PARTITION BY rt.month ORDER BY rt.year) AS prev_cities_added,
    LAG(rt.running_total) OVER (PARTITION BY rt.month ORDER BY rt.year) AS prev_running_total
  FROM running_totals rt
)
SELECT
  year,
  CASE month
    WHEN '04' THEN 'April'
    WHEN '05' THEN 'May'
    WHEN '06' THEN 'June'
    ELSE month
  END AS month,
  cities_added AS monthly_total,
  running_total AS cumulative_running_total,
  CASE
    WHEN prev_cities_added IS NOT NULL AND prev_cities_added > 0
      THEN ROUND(100.0 * (cities_added - prev_cities_added) / prev_cities_added, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS yoy_growth_monthly_total_pct,
  CASE
    WHEN prev_running_total IS NOT NULL AND prev_running_total > 0
      THEN ROUND(100.0 * (running_total - prev_running_total) / prev_running_total, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS yoy_growth_cumulative_running_total_pct
FROM growth_calc
WHERE year IN ('2022', '2023')
ORDER BY year, month
```

```sql
WITH top_customers AS (
    SELECT customer_id
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
    ORDER BY SUM(amount) DESC
    LIMIT 10
),
monthly_payments AS (
    SELECT
        p.customer_id,
        CAST(STRFTIME('%Y-%m', p.payment_date) AS TEXT) AS year_month,
        SUM(p.amount) AS monthly_amount
    FROM payment p
    JOIN top_customers tc ON p.customer_id = tc.customer_id
    GROUP BY p.customer_id, year_month
),
monthly_changes AS (
    SELECT
        mp.customer_id,
        mp.year_month,
        mp.monthly_amount,
        LAG(mp.monthly_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY mp.customer_id ORDER BY mp.year_month) AS prev_monthly_amount
    FROM monthly_payments mp
),
differences AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        year_month,
        ROUND(ABS(monthly_amount - prev_monthly_amount), 2) AS diff
    FROM monthly_changes
    WHERE prev_monthly_amount IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    year_month,
    diff AS max_monthly_difference
FROM differences
ORDER BY diff DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
WITH player_runs AS (
    SELECT 
        pm.player_id,
        SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS total_runs,
        COUNT(DISTINCT pm.match_id) AS matches_played
    FROM player_match pm
    JOIN batsman_scored bs ON pm.match_id = bs.match_id AND pm.player_id = bs.player_id
    GROUP BY pm.player_id
),
player_avg AS (
    SELECT
        pr.player_id,
        CAST(pr.total_runs AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(pr.matches_played, 0) AS avg_runs_per_match
    FROM player_runs pr
    WHERE pr.matches_played > 0
),
player_country AS (
    SELECT 
        p.player_id,
        p.country_name
    FROM player p
),
country_player_avgs AS (
    SELECT
        pc.country_name,
        pa.avg_runs_per_match
    FROM player_avg pa
    JOIN player_country pc ON pa.player_id = pc.player_id
)
SELECT
    country_name,
    AVG(avg_runs_per_match) AS country_batting_avg
FROM country_player_avgs
GROUP BY country_name
ORDER BY country_batting_avg DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

```sql
WITH batsman_runs AS (
  SELECT 
    m.season_id,
    bb.striker AS player_id,
    SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS total_runs
  FROM 
    ball_by_ball bb
    JOIN batsman_scored bs USING (match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no)
    JOIN match m ON bb.match_id = m.match_id
  GROUP BY m.season_id, bb.striker
),
TopBatsmen AS (
  SELECT 
    season_id,
    player_id,
    total_runs,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY season_id 
      ORDER BY total_runs DESC, player_id ASC
    ) AS rn
  FROM batsman_runs
),
filtered_wickets AS (
  SELECT 
    m.season_id,
    bb.bowler AS player_id
  FROM 
    ball_by_ball bb
    JOIN wicket_taken wt USING (match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no)
    JOIN match m ON bb.match_id = m.match_id
  WHERE wt.kind_out NOT IN ('run out', 'hit wicket', 'retired hurt')
),
bowler_wickets AS (
  SELECT 
    season_id,
    player_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_wickets
  FROM filtered_wickets
  GROUP BY season_id, player_id
),
TopBowlers AS (
  SELECT 
    season_id,
    player_id,
    total_wickets,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY season_id 
      ORDER BY total_wickets DESC, player_id ASC
    ) AS rn
  FROM bowler_wickets
),
SelectedBatsmen AS (
  SELECT * FROM TopBatsmen WHERE rn <= 3
),
SelectedBowlers AS (
  SELECT * FROM TopBowlers WHERE rn <= 3
)
SELECT
  sb.season_id,
  sb.player_id AS batsman_id,
  p1.player_name AS batsman_name,
  sb.total_runs,
  sw.player_id AS bowler_id,
  p2.player_name AS bowler_name,
  sw.total_wickets
FROM
  SelectedBatsmen sb
  JOIN SelectedBowlers sw
    ON sb.season_id = sw.season_id AND sb.rn = sw.rn
  JOIN player p1 ON sb.player_id = p1.player_id
  JOIN player p2 ON sw.player_id = p2.player_id
ORDER BY
  sb.season_id ASC, sb.rn ASC
```

```sql
WITH
-- Join sales to times, customers, countries to get US, quarter info, and city
sales_with_context AS (
  SELECT
    s.cust_id,
    cu.cust_city AS city,
    s.prod_id,
    s.amount_sold,
    t.calendar_year,
    t.calendar_quarter_number,
    s.promo_id
  FROM sales s
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  JOIN customers cu ON s.cust_id = cu.cust_id
  JOIN countries co ON cu.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'United States'
    AND ((t.calendar_year = 2019 AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4)
         OR (t.calendar_year = 2020 AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4))
    AND s.promo_id = 0
),

-- City sales per quarter (2019 Q4 and 2020 Q4 only, no promotion)
city_quarter_sales AS (
  SELECT city, calendar_year, SUM(amount_sold) AS total_sales
  FROM sales_with_context
  GROUP BY city, calendar_year
),

-- Select cities with at least 20% increase from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020
cities_growth AS (
  SELECT a.city, a.total_sales AS sales_2019, b.total_sales AS sales_2020
  FROM 
    (SELECT city, total_sales FROM city_quarter_sales WHERE calendar_year = 2019) a
    INNER JOIN 
    (SELECT city, total_sales FROM city_quarter_sales WHERE calendar_year = 2020) b
    ON a.city = b.city
  WHERE a.total_sales > 0 AND (b.total_sales - a.total_sales) * 1.0 / a.total_sales >= 0.2
),

-- All relevant sales in those cities in Q4 of 2019 and 2020 (no promotion)
filtered_sales AS (
  SELECT swc.*
  FROM sales_with_context swc
  JOIN cities_growth cg ON swc.city = cg.city
),

-- Product total sales (in all those cities, over both Q4 periods)
product_sales_total AS (
  SELECT prod_id, SUM(amount_sold) AS sales_total
  FROM filtered_sales
  GROUP BY prod_id
),

-- Rank products by overall sales and top 20% cutoff (ties included)
ranked_products AS (
  SELECT prod_id, sales_total,
         RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sales_total DESC) AS rnk,
         COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_products
  FROM product_sales_total
),
top_20pct_products AS (
  SELECT prod_id
  FROM ranked_products
  WHERE rnk <= CAST(total_products * 0.2 + 0.9999 AS INTEGER)
),

-- Sales by product per quarter for the top group
top_product_sales_by_year AS (
  SELECT fs.prod_id, fs.calendar_year, SUM(fs.amount_sold) AS prod_sales
  FROM filtered_sales fs
  JOIN top_20pct_products tp ON fs.prod_id = tp.prod_id
  GROUP BY fs.prod_id, fs.calendar_year
),

total_sales_by_year AS (
  SELECT calendar_year, SUM(amount_sold) AS total_sales
  FROM filtered_sales
  GROUP BY calendar_year
),

-- Share of each top product on each year
product_share_by_year AS (
  SELECT tps.prod_id, tps.calendar_year, tps.prod_sales * 1.0 / tsby.total_sales AS share
  FROM top_product_sales_by_year tps
  JOIN total_sales_by_year tsby ON tps.calendar_year = tsby.calendar_year
),

-- Reshape and calculate share changes
product_share_change AS (
  SELECT
    p.prod_id,
    p2019.share AS share_2019,
    p2020.share AS share_2020,
    (p2020.share - p2019.share) AS share_change
  FROM
    (SELECT * FROM product_share_by_year WHERE calendar_year = 2019) p2019
    JOIN (SELECT * FROM product_share_by_year WHERE calendar_year = 2020) p2020
      ON p2019.prod_id = p2020.prod_id
    JOIN products p ON p2019.prod_id = p.prod_id
)
SELECT psc.prod_id, pr.prod_name, psc.share_2019, psc.share_2020, psc.share_change
FROM product_share_change psc
JOIN products pr ON psc.prod_id = pr.prod_id
ORDER BY psc.share_change DESC
LIMIT 1000
```

```sql
  JOIN countries c ON s.country_id = c.country_id
  WHERE c.country_name = 'United States'
    AND ((t.year = 2019 AND t.quarter = 4) OR (t.year = 2020 AND t.quarter = 4))
    AND (s.promotion_id IS NULL OR s.promotion_id NOT IN (
      SELECT promotion_id FROM promotions
    ))
),

-- 2. City sales by quarter (exclude promotion sales)
city_quarter_sales AS (
  SELECT
    city,
    year,
    SUM(amount) AS total_sales
  FROM sales_with_context
  GROUP BY city, year
),

-- 3. Cities with >=20% sales growth from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020
city_growth AS (
  SELECT
    c2019.city,
    c2019.total_sales AS sales_2019,
    c2020.total_sales AS sales_2020,
    ((c2020.total_sales - c2019.total_sales) * 1.0 / NULLIF(c2019.total_sales, 0)) AS growth_rate
  FROM
    (SELECT city, total_sales FROM city_quarter_sales WHERE year = 2019) c2019
    JOIN
    (SELECT city, total_sales FROM city_quarter_sales WHERE year = 2020) c2020
    ON c2019.city = c2020.city
  WHERE
    c2019.total_sales > 0
    AND ((c2020.total_sales - c2019.total_sales) * 1.0 / c2019.total_sales) >= 0.2
),

-- 4. All non-promo sales in the selected cities, Q4 2019 and Q4 2020
selected_city_sales AS (
  SELECT swc.*
  FROM sales_with_context swc
  JOIN city_growth cg ON swc.city = cg.city
),

-- 5. Total sales by product across all selected cities, Q4 2019 + Q4 2020
product_sales_total AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    SUM(amount) AS sales_total
  FROM selected_city_sales
  GROUP BY product_id
),

-- 6. Rank products by overall sales, choose top 20%
top_products AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sales_total DESC) AS rnk,
    COUNT(*) OVER () AS prod_cnt,
    sales_total
  FROM product_sales_total
),
top_20pc_products AS (
  SELECT product_id
  FROM top_products
  WHERE rnk <= CAST(prod_cnt * 0.2 + 0.9999 AS INTEGER) -- ceil
),

top_prod_by_year AS (
  SELECT
    s.product_id,
    s.year,
    SUM(s.amount) AS prod_sales
  FROM selected_city_sales s
  JOIN top_20pc_products tp ON s.product_id = tp.product_id
  GROUP BY s.product_id, s.year
),

  SELECT

  SELECT
    tpy.product_id,
    tpy.year,
    tpy.prod_sales * 1.0 / NULLIF(asy.total_amt, 0) AS share
  FROM top_prod_by_year tpy

)

SELECT

  share_2020,
  share_change
FROM product_share_change p
JOIN products pr ON pr.product_id = p.product_id
ORDER BY share_change DESC;
```

```sql
WITH ordered_cities AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng
    ) AS rn
  FROM (
    SELECT
      geolocation_state,
      geolocation_city,
      geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
      AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
      AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng
    FROM olist_geolocation
    GROUP BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix
  )
),
city_pairs AS (
  SELECT
    curr.geolocation_state AS state1,
    curr.geolocation_city AS city1,
    curr.geolocation_zip_code_prefix AS zip1,
    curr.geolocation_lat AS lat1,
    curr.geolocation_lng AS lng1,
    prev.geolocation_state AS state2,
    prev.geolocation_city AS city2,
    prev.geolocation_zip_code_prefix AS zip2,
    prev.geolocation_lat AS lat2,
    prev.geolocation_lng AS lng2,
    6371 * ACOS(
      COS(RADIANS(curr.geolocation_lat)) * COS(RADIANS(prev.geolocation_lat)) *
      COS(RADIANS(prev.geolocation_lng) - RADIANS(curr.geolocation_lng)) +
      SIN(RADIANS(curr.geolocation_lat)) * SIN(RADIANS(prev.geolocation_lat))
    ) AS distance_km
  FROM ordered_cities curr
  JOIN ordered_cities prev ON curr.rn = prev.rn + 1
)
SELECT
  state1, city1, zip1, lat1, lng1,
  state2, city2, zip2, lat2, lng2,
  distance_km
FROM city_pairs
ORDER BY distance_km DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
  FROM city
  WHERE city LIKE 'A%' OR city LIKE '%-%'

)

FROM rental_film_category rfc
```

WITH qualified_cities AS (
  SELECT city_id
  FROM city
  WHERE city LIKE 'A%' OR city LIKE '%-%'
),
qualified_customers AS (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM customer
  JOIN address ON customer.address_id = address.address_id
  WHERE address.city_id IN (SELECT city_id FROM qualified_cities)
),
rentals_with_duration AS (
  SELECT
    r.rental_id,
    r.inventory_id,
    JULIANDAY(r.return_date) - JULIANDAY(r.rental_date) AS rental_hours,
    r.customer_id
  FROM rental r
  WHERE r.return_date IS NOT NULL
    AND r.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM qualified_customers)
),
rental_film_category AS (
  SELECT
    rw.rental_hours * 24 AS rental_hours, -- convert days to hours
    fc.category_id
  FROM rentals_with_duration rw
  JOIN inventory i ON rw.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id
)
SELECT c.name AS category_name, SUM(rfc.rental_hours) AS total_rental_hours
FROM rental_film_category rfc
JOIN category c ON rfc.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
ORDER BY total_rental_hours DESC
LIMIT 1;

```sql
WITH female_legislators AS (
  SELECT l.id_bioguide
  FROM legislators l
  WHERE l.gender = 'F'
),
first_state_per_legislator AS (
  SELECT lt.id_bioguide, lt.state, MIN(lt.term_start) AS first_term_start
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  GROUP BY lt.id_bioguide
),
terms_including_dec31 AS (
  SELECT 
    lt.id_bioguide
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM (
      SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start) AS INTEGER) AS year_start,
             CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_end) AS INTEGER) AS year_end
    ) years,
    (
      SELECT 0 AS offset UNION SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5
      UNION SELECT 6 UNION SELECT 7 UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9 UNION SELECT 10
      UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12 UNION SELECT 13 UNION SELECT 14 UNION SELECT 15
      UNION SELECT 16 UNION SELECT 17 UNION SELECT 18 UNION SELECT 19 UNION SELECT 20
    ) o
    WHERE (year_start + o.offset) BETWEEN year_start AND year_end
      AND (
        DATE((year_start + o.offset) || '-12-31') BETWEEN lt.term_start AND lt.term_end
      )
    LIMIT 1
  )

GROUP BY fsp.state
ORDER BY female_legislator_count DESC
```

  FROM legislators l
  WHERE l.gender = 'F'

),

```sql
  SELECT
    lt.legislator_id
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM (
      -- Generate a list of every year in this term
      SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.start_date) AS INTEGER) AS year_start,
             CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.end_date) AS INTEGER) AS year_end
    ) years,
    -- Expand for each year the term covers, including both start and end
    (
      SELECT 0 AS offset UNION SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5
      UNION SELECT 6 UNION SELECT 7 UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9 UNION SELECT 10
      UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12 UNION SELECT 13 UNION SELECT 14 UNION SELECT 15
      UNION SELECT 16 UNION SELECT 17 UNION SELECT 18 UNION SELECT 19 UNION SELECT 20
      -- covers up to 21-year terms
    ) o
    WHERE (year_start + o.offset) BETWEEN year_start AND year_end
      AND (
        DATE((year_start + o.offset) || '-12-31') BETWEEN lt.start_date AND lt.end_date
      )
    LIMIT 1
  )
)

JOIN terms_including_dec31 tic ON fl.id = tic.legislator_id
GROUP BY fsp.state
ORDER BY female_legislator_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

  SELECT 
    lt.id_bioguide
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM (
      SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start) AS INTEGER) AS year_start,
             CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_end) AS INTEGER) AS year_end
    ) years,
    (
      SELECT 0 AS offset UNION SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5
      UNION SELECT 6 UNION SELECT 7 UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9 UNION SELECT 10
      UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12 UNION SELECT 13 UNION SELECT 14 UNION SELECT 15
      UNION SELECT 16 UNION SELECT 17 UNION SELECT 18 UNION SELECT 19 UNION SELECT 20
    ) o
    WHERE (year_start + o.offset) BETWEEN year_start AND year_end
      AND (

    LIMIT 1
  )
)

JOIN terms_including_dec31 tic ON fl.id_bioguide = tic.id_bioguide
GROUP BY fsp.state
ORDER BY female_legislator_count DESC
LIMIT 1;

```sql
WITH txn_monthly AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date)) AS month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS net_amount
    FROM
        customer_transactions
    GROUP BY
        customer_id, month
),
txn_cumsum AS (
    SELECT
        t1.customer_id,
        t1.month,
        SUM(t2.net_amount) AS closing_balance
    FROM
        txn_monthly t1
        JOIN txn_monthly t2
          ON t1.customer_id = t2.customer_id
         AND t2.month <= t1.month
    GROUP BY
        t1.customer_id, t1.month
),
latest_months AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        month AS latest_month,
        closing_balance AS latest_balance,
        LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month) AS prev_balance
    FROM
        txn_cumsum
),
most_recent_month AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        latest_month,
        latest_balance,
        prev_balance
    FROM (
        SELECT
            *,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY latest_month DESC) as rn
        FROM latest_months
    ) sub
    WHERE rn = 1
),
growth_rates AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        CASE
            WHEN IFNULL(prev_balance, 0) = 0 THEN latest_balance * 100
            ELSE ((latest_balance - prev_balance) * 1.0 / ABS(prev_balance)) * 100
        END AS growth_rate
    FROM
        most_recent_month
)
SELECT
    (SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*)) * 100 AS pct_customers_growth_over_5
FROM
    growth_rates;
```

```sql
WITH driver_yearly_points AS (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    ds.driver_id,
    d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_full_name,
    SUM(ds.points) AS total_points
  FROM driver_standings ds

  JOIN drivers d ON ds.driver_id = d.driver_id
  GROUP BY r.year, ds.driver_id
),
max_driver_points AS (

  FROM driver_yearly_points
  GROUP BY year

  SELECT
    dyp.year,
    dyp.driver_full_name,
    dyp.total_points
  FROM driver_yearly_points dyp
  JOIN max_driver_points mdp ON dyp.year = mdp.year AND dyp.total_points = mdp.max_points
),
constructor_yearly_points AS (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    cs.constructor_id,
    c.name AS constructor_name,
    SUM(cs.points) AS total_points
  FROM constructor_standings cs
  JOIN races r ON cs.race_id = r.race_id
  JOIN constructors c ON cs.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
  GROUP BY r.year, cs.constructor_id
),
max_constructor_points AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    MAX(total_points) AS max_points
  FROM constructor_yearly_points
  GROUP BY year
),
top_constructors AS (
  SELECT

)

  tc.constructor_name AS top_constructor,
```

```sql
WITH ActorYears AS (
  SELECT
    M_Cast.PID,
    CAST(Movie.year AS INTEGER) AS yr
  FROM
    M_Cast
    JOIN Movie ON M_Cast.MID = Movie.MID
  GROUP BY
    M_Cast.PID, yr
),
ActorYearRange AS (
  SELECT
    PID,
    MIN(yr) AS min_year,
    MAX(yr) AS max_year
  FROM
    ActorYears
  GROUP BY
    PID
),
YearSeries AS (
  SELECT
    a.PID,
    y AS yr
  FROM
    ActorYearRange a
    JOIN (
      SELECT 1900 + n AS y FROM (
        SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER () - 1 AS n FROM (
          SELECT 1 FROM M_Cast LIMIT 201
        )
      ) WHERE n <= 200
    ) years
    ON y BETWEEN a.min_year AND a.max_year
),
ActorYearMatrix AS (
  SELECT
    ys.PID,
    ys.yr,
    CASE WHEN ay.yr IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_credit
  FROM
    YearSeries ys
    LEFT JOIN ActorYears ay
      ON ys.PID = ay.PID AND ys.yr = ay.yr
),
ActorGaps AS (
  SELECT
    a.PID,
    a.yr AS gap_start
  FROM
    ActorYearMatrix a
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM ActorYearMatrix b
      WHERE b.PID = a.PID AND b.yr BETWEEN a.yr AND a.yr+3 AND b.has_credit = 1
    )
),
ActorsWithBadGaps AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT PID FROM ActorGaps
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.PID) AS num_actors_without_long_gaps
FROM ActorYears a
WHERE a.PID NOT IN (SELECT PID FROM ActorsWithBadGaps)
;
```

```sql
WITH team_season_goals AS (
  SELECT
    t.team_api_id,
    m.season,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN t.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id THEN m.home_team_goal
        WHEN t.team_api_id = m.away_team_api_id THEN m.away_team_goal
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS season_goals
  FROM
    Team t
    JOIN Match m ON t.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id OR t.team_api_id = m.away_team_api_id
  GROUP BY
    t.team_api_id,
    m.season
),
team_max_season_goals AS (
  SELECT
    team_api_id,
    MAX(season_goals) AS max_season_goals
  FROM
    team_season_goals
  GROUP BY
    team_api_id
),
ordered_goals AS (
  SELECT
    max_season_goals,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY max_season_goals) AS rn,
    COUNT(*) OVER () AS total
  FROM
    team_max_season_goals
)
SELECT
  AVG(max_season_goals) AS median_max_season_goals
FROM
  ordered_goals
WHERE
  rn = (total + 1) / 2
  OR rn = (total + 2) / 2;
```

```sql
        MIN(DATE(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date))) as min_month,
        MAX(DATE(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date))) as max_month
    FROM customer_transactions
), month_list AS (
    -- Generate list of months between min and max
    WITH RECURSIVE ml(month) AS (
        SELECT min_month FROM months
        UNION ALL
        SELECT DATE(strftime('%Y-%m-01', DATE(month, '+1 month')))
        FROM ml, months
        WHERE month < max_month
    )
    SELECT month FROM ml
), customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
), customer_months AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id, 
        m.month
    FROM customers c
    CROSS JOIN month_list m
), txn_months AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id, 
        DATE(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date)) as month, 
        SUM(txn_amount) as month_change
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id, month
), month_balances AS (
    SELECT
        cm.customer_id,
        cm.month,
        COALESCE(tm.month_change, 0) as month_change
    FROM customer_months cm
    LEFT JOIN txn_months tm
        ON cm.customer_id = tm.customer_id AND cm.month = tm.month
), ordered AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        month,
        month_change,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month) as rn
    FROM month_balances
), initial_balance AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        IFNULL(SUM(txn_amount), 0) as start_balance
    FROM customer_transactions
    WHERE txn_date < (SELECT min_month FROM months)
    GROUP BY customer_id
), cumulative AS (

        o.month,

    FROM ordered o
    LEFT JOIN initial_balance ib ON o.customer_id = ib.customer_id
)
```

```sql
WITH jan_inserts AS (

        ci.city_id,

    WHERE date(a.type) >= '2022-01-01' AND date(a.type) <= '2022-01-31'
),
country_days AS (
    SELECT
        ci.country_code_2,
        COUNT(DISTINCT insert_date) AS days_with_data
    FROM jan_inserts ci
    GROUP BY ci.country_code_2
    HAVING days_with_data = 9
),
target_country AS (
    SELECT country_code_2 FROM country_days LIMIT 1
),
country_jan AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM jan_inserts
    WHERE country_code_2 = (SELECT country_code_2 FROM target_country)
),
dates_list AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT insert_date FROM country_jan
),
ordered_days AS (
    SELECT
        insert_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY insert_date) AS rn
    FROM dates_list
),
grp_days AS (
    SELECT
        insert_date,
        DATE(insert_date, '-'||(rn)||' days') AS gap_grp
    FROM ordered_days
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT
        gap_grp,
        MIN(insert_date) AS streak_start,
        MAX(insert_date) AS streak_end,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM grp_days
    GROUP BY gap_grp
),
longest_streak AS (
    SELECT *

    ORDER BY streak_length DESC, streak_start
    LIMIT 1
),

)
```

```sql
WITH jan_inserts AS (
    SELECT
        a.city_id,
        a.insert_date,
        DATE(a.insert_date) AS dt
    FROM aliens a
    WHERE a.insert_date >= '2022-01-01' AND a.insert_date < '2022-02-01'
),
city_country AS (
    SELECT
        c.id AS city_id,
        c.name AS city_name,
        cc.country
    FROM cities c
    JOIN cities_countries cc ON c.id = cc.city_id
),
-- Find which country has entries on exactly 9 distinct days in Jan 2022
country_days AS (
    SELECT
        cc.country,
        COUNT(DISTINCT j.dt) AS days_with_entries
    FROM jan_inserts j
    JOIN city_country cc ON j.city_id = cc.city_id
    GROUP BY cc.country
    HAVING days_with_entries = 9
),
-- Now, get that country's city_ids and capital
country_cities AS (
    SELECT
        cc.country,
        cc.city_id,
        cc.city_name,
        c.capital
    FROM city_country cc
    JOIN (
        SELECT country FROM country_days
    ) cd ON cc.country = cd.country
    JOIN cities c ON c.id = cc.city_id
),
country_jan_inserts AS (
    SELECT
        j.city_id,
        c.country,
        j.dt
    FROM jan_inserts j
    JOIN country_cities c ON j.city_id = c.city_id
),
-- Find all unique days with inserts for this country in Jan 2022
distinct_days AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT dt FROM country_jan_inserts
),
-- Find longest consecutive streak from these days
numbered_days AS (
    SELECT
        dt,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY dt) AS rn
    FROM distinct_days
),
day_groups AS (
    SELECT
        dt,
        DATE(dt, '-' || (rn) || ' days') AS group_id
    FROM numbered_days
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT
        group_id,
        MIN(dt) AS start_dt,
        MAX(dt) AS end_dt,
        COUNT(*) AS days_count
    FROM day_groups
    GROUP BY group_id
),
longest_streak AS (
    SELECT * FROM streaks ORDER BY days_count DESC, start_dt LIMIT 1
),
inserts_in_streak AS (
    SELECT
        cji.*,
        c.city_name,
        c.capital
    FROM country_jan_inserts cji
    JOIN country_cities c ON cji.city_id = c.city_id
    JOIN longest_streak ls ON cji.dt >= ls.start_dt AND cji.dt <= ls.end_dt
),
capital_id AS (
    SELECT city_id FROM country_cities WHERE capital = 1
),
final_counts AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS total_entries,
        SUM(CASE WHEN i.city_id IN (SELECT city_id FROM capital_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS capital_entries
    FROM inserts_in_streak i
)
SELECT
    (capital_entries * 1.0) / total_entries AS capital_entry_proportion
FROM final_counts;
```

```sql
WITH bowler_balls AS (
    SELECT
        b.bowler_id,
        b.match_id,
        COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    WHERE b.extra_type IS NULL -- Only legal deliveries, ignoring wides/no-balls
    GROUP BY b.bowler_id, b.match_id
),
bowler_runs AS (
    SELECT
        b.bowler_id,
        b.match_id,
        SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS runs_conceded
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    JOIN batsman_scored bs ON b.match_id = bs.match_id AND b.inning_no = bs.inning_no AND b.over_id = bs.over_id AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
    WHERE b.extra_type IS NULL -- Only runs scored off the bat, ignore extras
    GROUP BY b.bowler_id, b.match_id
),
bowler_wickets AS (
    SELECT
        b.bowler_id,
        b.match_id,
        COUNT(*) AS wickets
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    JOIN wicket_taken w ON
        b.match_id = w.match_id AND b.inning_no = w.inning_no AND b.over_id = w.over_id AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id
    WHERE w.dismissal_type NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field') -- Only wickets credited to the bowler
    GROUP BY b.bowler_id, b.match_id
),
bowler_agg AS (
    SELECT
        b.bowler_id,
        SUM(w.wickets) AS total_wickets,
        SUM(bb.balls_bowled) AS total_balls,
        SUM(br.runs_conceded) AS total_runs
    FROM
        (SELECT DISTINCT bowler_id, match_id FROM ball_by_ball) b
        LEFT JOIN bowler_balls bb ON b.bowler_id = bb.bowler_id AND b.match_id = bb.match_id
        LEFT JOIN bowler_runs br ON b.bowler_id = br.bowler_id AND b.match_id = br.match_id
        LEFT JOIN bowler_wickets w ON b.bowler_id = w.bowler_id AND b.match_id = w.match_id
    GROUP BY b.bowler_id
),
best_performance AS (
    SELECT
        b.bowler_id,
        bw.match_id,
        IFNULL(bw.wickets, 0) AS wickets,
        IFNULL(br.runs_conceded, 0) AS runs_conceded,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY b.bowler_id
            ORDER BY IFNULL(bw.wickets, 0) DESC, IFNULL(br.runs_conceded, 0) ASC
        ) AS rnk
    FROM
        (SELECT DISTINCT bowler_id, match_id FROM ball_by_ball) b
        LEFT JOIN bowler_wickets bw ON b.bowler_id = bw.bowler_id AND b.match_id = bw.match_id
        LEFT JOIN bowler_runs br ON b.bowler_id = br.bowler_id AND b.match_id = br.match_id
)
SELECT
    p.player_name AS bowler,
    ba.total_wickets,
    ROUND(
        CASE WHEN ba.total_balls > 0 THEN (CAST(ba.total_runs AS FLOAT) * 6) / ba.total_balls ELSE NULL END, 2
    ) AS economy_rate,
    ROUND(
        CASE WHEN ba.total_wickets > 0 THEN CAST(ba.total_balls AS FLOAT) / ba.total_wickets ELSE NULL END, 2
    ) AS strike_rate,
    printf('%d-%d', bp.wickets, bp.runs_conceded) AS best_bowling
FROM
    bowler_agg ba
    JOIN player p ON ba.bowler_id = p.player_id
    JOIN best_performance bp ON ba.bowler_id = bp.bowler_id
WHERE
    bp.rnk = 1
ORDER BY
    ba.total_wickets DESC, economy_rate ASC
;
```

# Special Words Definition

## Batting Average
- Batting average is a measure of a batsman's performance, calculated by dividing the total number of runs scored by the number of times they have been dismissed. A higher batting average indicates a more consistent and successful batsman.
- Batting Average = Total Runs ÷ Total Dismissals

## Strike Rate
- In batting, strike rate indicates the scoring rate of a batsman, showing the average number of runs scored per 100 balls faced. A higher strike rate reflects an aggressive and fast-scoring batsman.
- Strike Rate = (Total Runs ÷ Balls Faced) × 100

## Wickets Taken
- Wickets taken refers to the total number of times a bowler has successfully dismissed an opposing batsman. This statistic is a core measure of a bowler's effectiveness and impact on the game.

## Economy Rate
- Economy rate measures a bowler's efficiency by indicating the average number of runs conceded per over (6 balls) bowled. A lower economy rate shows greater control and efficiency in restricting the opposition's scoring.
- Economy Rate = (Total Runs Conceded ÷ Balls Bowled) × 6

## Wickets Taken
- The number of times a bowler successfully dismisses a batsman in a single match.  This metric is a direct indicator of the bowler's effectiveness, showing how many players they were able to remove from play.

## Runs Given
- The total number of runs scored by the batting side off a particular bowler’s deliveries in a single match.  This value reflects the runs the bowler has conceded to the batting team, and a lower runs-given value is typically favorable for the bowler's performance.

```sql
WITH film_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        f.film_id,
        f.title,
        SUM(p.amount) AS total_revenue
    FROM film f
    JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
    JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
    JOIN payment p ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
    GROUP BY f.film_id, f.title
),
film_actor_count AS (
    SELECT
        fa.film_id,
        COUNT(fa.actor_id) AS actor_count
    FROM film_actor fa
    GROUP BY fa.film_id
),
actor_film_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        fa.actor_id,
        fa.film_id,
        fr.title,
        fr.total_revenue,
        fr.total_revenue * 1.0 / fac.actor_count AS revenue_per_actor
    FROM film_actor fa
    JOIN film_revenue fr ON fa.film_id = fr.film_id
    JOIN film_actor_count fac ON fa.film_id = fac.film_id
),
ranked_films AS (
    SELECT
        afr.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY afr.actor_id ORDER BY afr.total_revenue DESC, afr.film_id) AS rn
    FROM actor_film_revenue afr
)
SELECT
    a.actor_id,
    a.first_name,
    a.last_name,
    rf.film_id,
    rf.title,
    rf.total_revenue,
    rf.revenue_per_actor,
    avg_top3.avg_revenue_per_actor
FROM actor a
JOIN (
    SELECT
        actor_id,
        AVG(revenue_per_actor) AS avg_revenue_per_actor
    FROM (
        SELECT
            afr.actor_id,
            afr.revenue_per_actor,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY afr.actor_id ORDER BY afr.total_revenue DESC, afr.film_id) AS rn
        FROM actor_film_revenue afr
    )
```

```sql
WITH inventory_fifo AS (
    SELECT
        i.product_id,
        i.location_id,
        i.available_qty,
        pch.purchase_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY i.product_id
            ORDER BY pch.purchase_date, i.available_qty
        ) AS fifo_rank
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN purchases pch ON i.purchase_id = pch.purchase_id
),
order_picks AS (
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        ol.product_id,
        ol.ordered_qty,
        inv.location_id,
        inv.available_qty,
        inv.purchase_date,
        inv.fifo_rank,
        LEAST(
            ol.ordered_qty -
                IFNULL(
                    SUM(ol2.ordered_qty) OVER (
                        PARTITION BY ol.order_id, ol.product_id
                        ORDER BY inv.purchase_date, inv.available_qty
                        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
                    ),
                    0
                ),
            inv.available_qty
        ) AS picked_qty
    FROM orderlines ol
    JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN inventory_fifo inv ON ol.product_id = inv.product_id
    WHERE
        (ol.ordered_qty -
            IFNULL(
                SUM(ol2.ordered_qty) OVER (
                    PARTITION BY ol.order_id, ol.product_id
                    ORDER BY inv.purchase_date, inv.available_qty
                    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
                ),
                0
            )
        ) > 0
),
order_pick_pct AS (
    SELECT
        op.product_id,
        op.order_id,
        SUM(
            CASE WHEN op.picked_qty > 0 THEN op.picked_qty ELSE 0 END
        ) AS total_picked,
        MAX(op.ordered_qty) AS total_ordered
    FROM order_picks op
    GROUP BY op.order_id, op.product_id
)
SELECT
    pr.product_name,
    AVG(CAST(opp.total_picked AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(opp.total_ordered, 0)) AS avg_pick_pct
FROM order_pick_pct opp
JOIN products pr ON opp.product_id = pr.product_id
GROUP BY pr.product_name
ORDER BY pr.product_name;
```

```sql
WITH session_pages AS (
    SELECT
        session,
        MIN(stamp) AS first_ts,
        MAX(stamp) AS last_ts
    FROM activity_log
    GROUP BY session
),

    SELECT
        a.session,
        a.path
    FROM activity_log a
    JOIN session_pages sp
        ON a.session = sp.session AND a.stamp = sp.first_ts
),
exit_pages AS (
    SELECT
        a.session,
        a.path
    FROM activity_log a
    JOIN session_pages sp
        ON a.session = sp.session AND a.stamp = sp.last_ts
),
landing_exit_union AS (
    SELECT session, path FROM landing_pages
    UNION
    SELECT session, path FROM exit_pages
)
SELECT
    path AS page,
    COUNT(DISTINCT session) AS unique_session_count
FROM landing_exit_union
GROUP BY page
ORDER BY unique_session_count DESC, page;
```

```sql
    player_id,
    debut,
    final_game
  FROM player
  WHERE debut IS NOT NULL AND final_game IS NOT NULL
),
career_spans AS (
  SELECT
    player_id,
    ROUND(ABS(CAST(strftime('%Y', final_game) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', debut) AS INTEGER)), 2) AS years_diff,
    ROUND(ABS(CAST(strftime('%m', final_game) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%m', debut) AS INTEGER)), 2) AS months_diff,
    ROUND(ABS(CAST(strftime('%d', final_game) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%d', debut) AS INTEGER)), 2) AS days_diff
  FROM player_dates
),
career_span_floats AS (
  SELECT
```

```sql
WITH partnership_details AS (
    SELECT
        bb.match_id,
        bb.innings_no,
        bb.striker AS player_a,
        bb.non_striker AS player_b,
        SUM(CASE WHEN bs.match_id = bb.match_id AND bs.innings_no = bb.innings_no AND bs.over_id = bb.over_id AND bs.ball_id = bb.ball_id AND bb.striker = bs.match_id THEN bs.runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS player_a_runs,
        SUM(CASE WHEN bs.match_id = bb.match_id AND bs.innings_no = bb.innings_no AND bs.over_id = bb.over_id AND bs.ball_id = bb.ball_id AND bb.non_striker = bs.match_id THEN bs.runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS player_b_runs,
        COUNT(*) as balls_in_partnership -- surrogate partition key
    FROM
        ball_by_ball bb
    JOIN batsman_scored bs ON bb.match_id = bs.match_id AND bb.over_id = bs.over_id AND bb.ball_id = bs.ball_id AND bb.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    GROUP BY
        bb.match_id, bb.innings_no, bb.striker, bb.non_striker
),
partnership_scores AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        player_a,
        player_b,
        player_a_runs,
        player_b_runs,
        (player_a_runs + player_b_runs) AS partnership_runs
    FROM partnership_details
),
```

Based on monthly sales data starting in January 2016 and using a centered moving average to adjust for seasonality, which products had a seasonality-adjusted sales ratio that stayed consistently above 2 for every month in the year 2017?

Provided benchmark documentation:

# Explanation of Metrics

## 1. Sales-to-CMA Ratio
- **Definition**: This ratio compares actual sales to the centered moving average (CMA) of sales.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Centered Moving Average (CMA)**: The CMA is a smoothed value of sales calculated over a rolling 12-month period. It averages sales from the months before and after a given month, specifically using two overlapping windows (5 months before and 6 months after, and vice versa).
  - **Sales-to-CMA Ratio**: The ratio is computed by dividing the actual sales amount for a month by its corresponding CMA value. A ratio greater than 2 indicates that the actual sales are more than twice the smoothed average for that period, suggesting significantly higher-than-average sales.

## 2. 12-Month Overlapping Windows
- **Definition**: A method to smooth sales data over time by averaging values in a specified window.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Window Size**: The window spans 12 months, with the specific approach involving overlapping periods. 
  - **First Window**: For a given month, this window includes 5 months before and 6 months after.
  - **Second Window**: Another window includes 6 months before and 5 months after the given month.
  - **Averaging**: Sales data is averaged over these two overlapping windows to compute the CMA. This method smooths out fluctuations by considering both the past and future sales in the calculation.

## 3. Restriction to the 7th and 30th Months
- **Definition**: A filter applied to focus calculations within a specific range of months.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Time Range**: Only the months between the 7th and 30th time steps (which correspond to specific periods) are considered for calculating the CMA and ratio.
  - **Purpose**: This restriction is used to avoid edge effects in the data where the moving average might be less reliable (e.g., at the very beginning or end of the available data). By focusing on these months, the calculations are more stable and meaningful.

```sql
    FROM model m
    JOIN model_score ms
      ON m.name = ms.name AND m.version = ms.version AND m.step = ms.step
    WHERE m.step IN (1,2,3)
),
stack_scores AS (
    SELECT
        problem_name,
        version,
        step,
        test_score AS stack_test_score
    FROM model_scores
    WHERE model_name = 'Stack'
```

```sql
WITH stats AS (
    SELECT 
        AVG([loss_rate_%]) AS avg_loss_rate,
        AVG(([loss_rate_%] - (SELECT AVG([loss_rate_%]) FROM veg_loss_rate_df)) * ([loss_rate_%] - (SELECT AVG([loss_rate_%]) FROM veg_loss_rate_df))) AS var_loss_rate
    FROM veg_loss_rate_df
),

    SELECT 
        avg_loss_rate, 
        SQRT(var_loss_rate) AS std_loss_rate

        v.item_name,

        s.avg_loss_rate,
        s.std_loss_rate,
        CASE 
            WHEN v.[loss_rate_%] >= s.avg_loss_rate - s.std_loss_rate
             AND v.[loss_rate_%] <= s.avg_loss_rate + s.std_loss_rate THEN 'within_1std'
            WHEN v.[loss_rate_%] < s.avg_loss_rate - s.std_loss_rate THEN 'below_1std'
            ELSE 'above_1std'

    FROM veg_loss_rate_df v, stds s
)

    COUNT(CASE WHEN category = 'below_1std' THEN 1 END) AS count_below_1std,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN category = 'within_1std' THEN 1 END) AS count_within_1std,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN category = 'above_1std' THEN 1 END) AS count_above_1std
FROM classified;
```

Provided benchmark documentation:

# Flight Route Distance Calculation

## Introduction

This document describes the method used to calculate the distance between two cities for flight routes. The calculation is based on the Haversine formula, which is commonly used to find the shortest distance between two points on a sphere given their latitude and longitude. This method is especially useful for determining flight distances between airports located in different cities around the world.

## City and Coordinate Extraction

For each flight, the following data is obtained:

- **Departure city** (referred to as `from_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).
- **Arrival city** (referred to as `to_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).

The coordinates are extracted as decimal values, with longitude and latitude represented in degrees. This ensures that trigonometric operations can be applied during the distance calculation.

## Haversine Formula

The Haversine formula is used to calculate the great-circle distance between two points on a sphere using their latitude and longitude. The formula is given as:

\[
d = 2r \cdot \arcsin\left(\sqrt{\sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) + \cos(\phi_1) \cdot \cos(\phi_2) \cdot \sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \lambda}{2}\right)}\right)
\]

Where:

- \( d \) is the distance between the two points (in kilometers).

WITH airport_cities AS (
    SELECT 
        airport_code, 
        json_extract(city, '$.en') AS city_en,
        TRIM(SUBSTR(coordinates, 1, INSTR(coordinates, ',') - 1)) * 1.0 AS longitude,
        TRIM(SUBSTR(coordinates, INSTR(coordinates, ',') + 1)) * 1.0 AS latitude
    FROM airports_data
),
flight_city_pairs AS (
    SELECT
        f.flight_id,
        dep.city_en AS dep_city,
        arr.city_en AS arr_city,
        dep.longitude AS dep_long,
        dep.latitude AS dep_lat,
        arr.longitude AS arr_long,
        arr.latitude AS arr_lat
    FROM flights f
    JOIN airport_cities dep ON f.departure_airport = dep.airport_code
    JOIN airport_cities arr ON f.arrival_airport = arr.airport_code
    WHERE dep.city_en <> arr.city_en
),
city_pairs_dedup AS (
    SELECT
        flight_id,
        CASE WHEN dep_city < arr_city THEN dep_city ELSE arr_city END AS city1,
        CASE WHEN dep_city < arr_city THEN arr_city ELSE dep_city END AS city2,
        CASE WHEN dep_city < arr_city THEN dep_long ELSE arr_long END AS long1,
        CASE WHEN dep_city < arr_city THEN dep_lat ELSE arr_lat END AS lat1,
        CASE WHEN dep_city < arr_city THEN arr_long ELSE dep_long END AS long2,
        CASE WHEN dep_city < arr_city THEN arr_lat ELSE dep_lat END AS lat2
    FROM flight_city_pairs
),
pair_distances AS (
    SELECT
        city1, city2,
        2 * 6371 *
          ASIN(
            MIN(
              1,
              SQRT(
                POW(SIN(RADIANS(lat2-lat1)/2),2) +
                COS(RADIANS(lat1)) * COS(RADIANS(lat2)) *
                POW(SIN(RADIANS(long2-long1)/2),2)
              )
            )
          ) AS distance
    FROM city_pairs_dedup
),
all_pair_avg AS (
    SELECT
        city1,
        city2,
        AVG(distance) as avg_distance
    FROM (
        SELECT
            city1,
            city2,
            2 * 6371 *
              ASIN(
                MIN(
                  1,
                  SQRT(
                    POW(SIN(RADIANS(lat2-lat1)/2),2) +
                    COS(RADIANS(lat1)) * COS(RADIANS(lat2)) *
                    POW(SIN(RADIANS(long2-long1)/2),2)
                  )
                )
              ) AS distance
        FROM city_pairs_dedup
    )
    GROUP BY city1, city2
),
range_buckets AS (
    SELECT
        city1,
        city2,
        avg_distance,
        CASE
            WHEN avg_distance < 1000 THEN '0'
            WHEN avg_distance < 2000 THEN '1000'
            WHEN avg_distance < 3000 THEN '2000'
            WHEN avg_distance < 4000 THEN '3000'
            WHEN avg_distance < 5000 THEN '4000'
            WHEN avg_distance < 6000 THEN '5000'
            ELSE '6000+'
        END AS distance_range
    FROM all_pair_avg
),
range_counts AS (
    SELECT distance_range, COUNT(*) AS pair_count
    FROM range_buckets
    GROUP BY distance_range
)
SELECT pair_count
FROM range_counts
WHERE pair_count = (
    SELECT MIN(pair_count) FROM range_counts
)
LIMIT 1;

```sql
WITH seasons_since_2001 AS (
    SELECT year, season
    FROM seasons
    WHERE year >= 2001
),
driver_points AS (
    -- Aggregate total points per driver, per season
    SELECT s.year, d.driverId, r.constructorId, SUM(ds.points) AS total_points
    FROM seasons_since_2001 s
    JOIN races rc ON s.year = rc.year AND s.season = rc.year
    JOIN results r ON rc.raceId = r.raceId
    JOIN drivers d ON r.driverId = d.driverId
    JOIN driver_standings ds ON rc.raceId = ds.raceId AND ds.driverId = r.driverId
    GROUP BY s.year, d.driverId, r.constructorId
    HAVING total_points > 0
),
least_scorers AS (
    -- Per season, find the minimum points scored by any point-scoring driver and who achieved it
    SELECT year, MIN(total_points) AS min_points
    FROM driver_points
    GROUP BY year
),
least_scorers_constructors AS (
    -- For each season, get constructors where a driver scored the min points
    SELECT dp.year, dp.constructorId

    JOIN least_scorers ls ON dp.year = ls.year AND dp.total_points = ls.min_points
    GROUP BY dp.year, dp.constructorId
)

JOIN constructors c ON lsc.constructorId = c.constructorId
GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.name
```

```sql
WITH lap_data AS (
  SELECT 
    lt.race_id,
    lt.driver_id,
    lt.lap,
    lt.position,
    LAG(lt.position) OVER (PARTITION BY lt.race_id, lt.driver_id ORDER BY lt.lap) AS prev_position
  FROM lap_times lt
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pit_stops ps WHERE ps.race_id = lt.race_id
  )
),
overtake_candidates AS (
  -- Find for each lap and race, position changes indicating a driver is now behind another (new overtake state)
  SELECT
    curr.race_id,
    curr.lap,
    curr.driver_id AS overtaking_driver,
    prev.driver_id AS overtaken_driver,
    curr.position AS curr_position,
    prev.position AS prev_position,
    curr.prev_position AS overtaker_prev_position,
    prev.prev_position AS overtaken_prev_position
  FROM lap_data curr
  JOIN lap_data prev
    ON curr.race_id = prev.race_id
    AND curr.lap = prev.lap
    AND curr.driver_id <> prev.driver_id
    AND curr.position = prev.position + 1 -- curr is now behind prev
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM lap_data pl_curr
    JOIN lap_data pl_prev
      ON pl_curr.race_id = pl_prev.race_id
      AND pl_curr.lap = curr.lap - 1
      AND pl_prev.lap = curr.lap - 1
      AND pl_curr.driver_id = curr.driver_id
      AND pl_prev.driver_id = prev.driver_id
      AND pl_curr.position = pl_prev.position + 1
  )
),
pit_entry_overtakes AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    oc.race_id,
    oc.lap,
    oc.overtaking_driver,
    oc.overtaken_driver,
    'P' AS label
  FROM overtake_candidates oc
  INNER JOIN pit_stops ps
    ON ps.race_id = oc.race_id
    AND ps.driver_id = oc.overtaken_driver
    AND ps.lap = oc.lap
),
pit_exit_overtakes AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    oc.race_id,
    oc.lap,
    oc.overtaking_driver,
    oc.overtaken_driver,
    'P' AS label
  FROM overtake_candidates oc
  INNER JOIN pit_stops ps
    ON ps.race_id = oc.race_id
    AND ps.driver_id = oc.overtaken_driver
    AND ps.lap = oc.lap - 1
),
retirement_overtakes AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    oc.race_id,
    oc.lap,
    oc.overtaking_driver,
    oc.overtaken_driver,
    'R' AS label
  FROM overtake_candidates oc
  INNER JOIN retirements r
    ON r.race_id = oc.race_id
    AND r.driver_id = oc.overtaken_driver
    AND r.lap = oc.lap
),
start_overtakes AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    oc.race_id,
    oc.lap,
    oc.overtaking_driver,
    oc.overtaken_driver,
    'S' AS label
  FROM overtake_candidates oc
  INNER JOIN results res_over ON res_over.race_id = oc.race_id AND res_over.driver_id = oc.overtaking_driver
  INNER JOIN results res_ovek ON res_ovek.race_id = oc.race_id AND res_ovek.driver_id = oc.overtaken_driver
  WHERE oc.lap = 1 AND ABS(res_over.grid - res_ovek.grid) <= 2
),
labelled_overtakes AS (
  SELECT race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver, label FROM retirement_overtakes
  UNION
  SELECT race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver, label FROM pit_entry_overtakes
  UNION
  SELECT race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver, label FROM pit_exit_overtakes
  UNION
  SELECT race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver, label FROM start_overtakes
  UNION
  -- Track overtakes: not classed above
  SELECT
    oc.race_id,
    oc.lap,
    oc.overtaking_driver,
    oc.overtaken_driver,
    'T' AS label
  FROM overtake_candidates oc
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver FROM retirement_overtakes
    UNION
    SELECT race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver FROM pit_entry_overtakes
    UNION
    SELECT race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver FROM pit_exit_overtakes
    UNION
    SELECT race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver FROM start_overtakes
  ) labelled USING (race_id, lap, overtaking_driver, overtaken_driver)
  WHERE labelled.race_id IS NULL
)
SELECT
  label,
  COUNT(*) AS overtake_count
FROM labelled_overtakes
GROUP BY label
ORDER BY label
```
